hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact 32-entry, two-bit bimodal direction predictor indexed
by fetch PC[6:2], with unconditional direct-JAL prediction. Reset the
counters to weakly not taken (01). Use explicit clocked counter bits,
one asynchronous fetch-direction read, and old-state reads for
saturating updates. Do not add registered lookahead, a BTB, tags,
cached targets, global history, a return stack, or a pipeline stage.
The single architectural angle is eliminating recurring control
bubbles with minimal predictor logic on the current multiplier-isolated
champion; all existing arithmetic datapaths stay intact.

Positively predecode legal conditional BRANCH funct3 values and JAL
from raw imem_data. Derive their exact B/J displacement, but implement
the prediction target as one 19-bit WORD-address addition, rather
than a 32-bit byte-address adder followed by a wide range comparison.
Admit only source PCs with PC[31:20]==0 and PC[1:0]==0, and only
displacements with bit 1 zero. Form target_word modulo 2^19 as
{1'b0, PC[19:2]} plus the signed B/J displacement divided by four,
sign-extended to 19 bits. Require target_word[18]==0 and reconstruct
{12'b0, target_word[17:0], 2'b00}. For an admitted source, the JAL
displacement bounds place the mathematical sum in [-2^18, 2^19),
so the high bit rejects both negative and >=1-MiB targets without
any unsafe modular alias. This also covers the narrower B displacement.
Rejecting a candidate must select ordinary PC+4, leaving architectural
target calculation and misalignment traps in EX authoritative. Keep
the existing full-width sequential PC+4 and EX recovery arithmetic;
the shortening applies only to speculative B/J target generation.

Select the admitted target for conditional branches when the indexed
counter MSB is one, and for JAL unconditionally. Keep JALR sequential.
Prediction and direction lookup depend only on the registered fetch
PC, raw instruction and stored predictor state. There is no EX-update
bypass and no lookup indexed by a combinational recovery/next-PC value.
Advance PC to the selected prediction only when the current fetch is
accepted. Preserve PC on imem, load-use, data-memory and arithmetic
holds; an accepted EX correction retains priority over fetch holds.

Carry one predicted_transfer bit with the instruction through if_id_t
and id_ex_t. Since a prediction always uses the current instruction's
exact direct target, EX can recover on actual_transfer XOR
predicted_transfer rather than a wide next-PC comparison. Compute
actual_transfer from the existing forwarded branch outcome and jump
control, suppressing it on the existing misalignment fault. Correct
predictions keep the fetched successor. On mismatch recover to the
actual target when transferring, or the resolving instruction's own
PC+4 when falling through. Qualify correction with valid EX advance;
a branch held behind an older memory stall cannot redirect or retrain.
Preserve actual pc_next, link values, trap rules and operands for RVFI.

Isolate direction training from the resolving comparator by registering
a one-entry update transaction: valid, PC[6:2], and taken outcome.
Enqueue once per advancing valid legal nontrapping conditional branch;
on the following edge saturate the CURRENT indexed counter from the
registered transaction. Permit update and enqueue on the same edge,
and clear the transaction-valid bit when there is no new branch.
Consume a queued update once even if the pipeline subsequently stalls.
Lookup/update collisions use old state; never forward the live EX
outcome into the fetch read. Reset pending update state deterministically.
This confines branch-outcome fanout to the update register instead of
all table writes, while delayed learning affects accuracy only.

Keep correction out of the empty-EX early-divider launch cone. Continue
raw instruction decode during flush and kill work at state acceptance.
Supply imem-ready early-decode eligibility independently of correction,
and require registered empty EX, a validated DIV/REM, ready MEM and
available arithmetic units. An EX correction necessarily occupies EX,
so that mandatory empty-EX guard prevents a wrong-path early launch.
Select candidate operands/opcode by registered EX occupancy only.
Preserve divider launch latency, result protocol and liveness bounds.

Subtracting the model's 288,234 saved one-cycle corrections from
4,773,913 champion cycles projects 4,485,679 cycles and 133.76 iter/sec
at 60 MHz, roughly 6.4 percent higher fitness. Pipeline bubbles and
memory/arithmetic holds advance the update queue in clocks rather than
instruction events, and change stall phase; this projection is not a
measured result. Clearing 4.6 percent above 125.68 requires over
131.46128 iter/sec, implying about 58.97 MHz at that projected cycle
count: there is little clock margin. A standalone arithmetic check
exhausted all 524,288 aligned JAL word displacements at seven source
PCs spanning RAM boundaries and the midpoint, 3,670,016 cases total;
the high-bit admission rule and reconstructed targets matched exact
mathematical range/alignment checks in every case. Keep these boundary
properties covered in implementation tests, and rely on unchanged
Gowin timing and CoreMark measurement for acceptance. Preserve
nret=1, all external IO/RVFI ports, decoder legality, arithmetic and
every formal, cosim, CRC, marker, UART and bounds check.

title: Retime divider sign conversion across its existing register boundaries
motivation:
The champion scores 132.63 iterations/second at 63.318 MHz with
4,773,913 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path
runs from an ID/EX destination tag through decode forwarding into
div_unit.divisor_q, which captures a conditionally negated 32-bit
operand. The previous one-hot forwarding experiment exposed a
divider-to-signed-result path instead. Both paths append sign
conversion to another substantial combinational path. Earlier
micro_opt attempts addressed forwarding, launch qualification and
radix-4 recurrence; this proposal uses the existing divider state
boundaries to separate sign conversion from those critical paths.
LESSONS.md is absent; the micro_opt history and latest champion in
log.jsonl were reviewed before proposing this change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retime only the real divider's input and output sign conversions.
Keep its interface, early decode launch, eight busy clocks, two
radix-4 digits per busy clock, and start/busy/result-valid/accept
protocol unchanged. This is a local combinational logic retiming
within the existing execution unit, with no new pipeline stage or
additional instruction cycle.

At accepted launch, capture raw a into quotient_q and raw b into
divisor_q instead of computing their magnitudes before those
registers. Keep the existing remainder_negative_q = signed_op &&
a[31], quotient_negative_q = signed_op && (a[31] XOR b[31]) &&
(b != 0), and select_remainder_q. Add one divisor_negative_q flag
capturing signed_op && b[31]. These sign/control captures are
independent of the full-width magnitude computation.

During busy group zero, compute initial_a = remainder_negative_q
? (0 - quotient_q) : quotient_q and initial_b = divisor_negative_q
? (0 - divisor_q) : divisor_q, all at 32-bit width. Apply the existing
narrow initial radix-4 logic to initial_a's top nibble and initial_b's
magnitude, including the D >= 16 bypass. Specifically, initial D/2D/3D
use initial_b[3:0], both trial digits use initial_a[31:28], and the
bypass predicate is OR(initial_b[31:4]). Capture quotient_q =
{initial_a[27:0], quotient_nibble}, remainder_q =
{28'b0, remainder_nibble}, divisor_q = initial_b, and divisor_3x_q =
{2'b0,initial_b} + {1'b0,initial_b,1'b0} on that same group-zero edge.
Use explicit 34-bit widths for 3D. Groups one through seven then
execute the current full-width recurrence without changes. The
dividend's remaining bits must come from initial_a, not the raw
launch word. No normalization/preparation clock is added.

On group seven, register the selected unsigned q2/r2 magnitude in
result_magnitude_q instead of performing sign correction before
result capture. Drive the existing result port combinationally as
the conditional negation of this registered magnitude using the
existing captured quotient/remainder sign selection. Do not add a
busy/valid/start-controlled output-data mux. The architectural
result is available in the same result-valid cycle as before and
reaches EX/MEM on the same acceptance edge. Its magnitude and sign
flags must remain stable while result_valid is pending; a new
accepted start may replace sign flags only when the old result is
absent or simultaneously accepted. Reset the new flag and magnitude
register to zero, preserving reset cancellation and accept/start
overlap. Keep raw RVFI operand/metadata capture in EX unchanged.

Leave RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and their original registered
result/latency exactly unchanged. Confine all magnitude/sign
retiming to the real-arithmetic branch. Preserve signed truncation
toward zero, dividend-signed remainders, unsigned high-bit inputs,
INT_MIN/-1 and divide-by-zero quotient/remainder behavior. In
particular, retain quotient sign suppression for b=0: the natural
all-ones quotient must never be negated.

This removes the wide negate from forwarded decode-to-launch
capture and from the final two-digit recurrence-to-result capture.
Input normalization instead shares the existing narrow first group;
output correction runs from an already registered result. A scratch
prototype of this exact change passed the existing real divider and
complete pipeline cocotb suites, including eight-clock divider and
ten-cycle ready-bus retirement-gap checks. The unchanged Gowin flow
with the nret=1 FPGA wrapper measured 74.883/75.375/75.375 MHz for
placement options 0/1/2, median 75.375 MHz. It used 3,719 logic cells
and 805 registers, versus 3,704 and 804 in the champion, with unchanged
LUT-RAM/BSRAM/DSP counts. Its worst median-placement path was
18.561 ns inside the divider rather than sign conversion appended
to the early launch path. These are prototype measurements, not
claims of an orchestrator fitness result.

The prototype also passed full selftest RVFI trace cosim with and
without both random bus stalls. Canonical 2K CoreMark with both
stalls completed, retained exactly 4,773,913 marker-bracketed cycles
for ten iterations, matched all five CRCs and the required UART
validation literal, and reported no out-of-bounds access. ALTOPS
Verilator lint passed; complete formal remains an implementation
gate and is not claimed here.

At the measured unchanged cycle count, that median projects approximately
157.89 iterations/second, a 19.04-percent gain. Expect nineteen
percent higher fitness with medium confidence. The main risks are
group-zero negate-plus-3D timing, result correction feeding younger
decode/early launch, and exact preservation of signed corner cases
and pending-result stability. Acceptance at unchanged cycles requires
median Fmax above approximately 66.23 MHz. Preserve nret=1, all
external ports, decode defaults, RVFI/order/trap rules, arbitrary
bus waits, bounded progress and every evaluation invariant. Require
existing formal, real-arithmetic, trace cosim and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker checks and reproduce the median vendor timing.

dependencies and completion under data-memory backpressure.

title: Retime the divider around raw capture and one parallel radix-16 digit per clock
motivation:
The champion scores 132.63 iterations/sec at median 63.318 MHz and
4,773,913 marker-bracketed cycles. Its reported 21.522 ns worst path
crosses EX completion forwarding and decode and ends at the divider's
magnitude register. The alternate forwarding experiment also exposed
a 22.403 ns divider path. Operand preparation and the recurring
two-radix-4-step/sign-correction path now limit clock headroom.
LESSONS.md is absent; the structural experiment log was reviewed.
The earlier raw-capture attempt exposed the old four-binary-step
recurrence. The earlier radix-16 attempt reached 47.17 MHz but was
limited by forwarding and the then-combinational multiply/ALU path.
The current core has since isolated multiplication and registered
final execute operands, making a fully retimed radix-16 divider
promising on this new surrounding pipeline.

A scratch prototype of the specified capture/prepare/digit structure
passed all six real-divider cocotb tests and all 24 pipeline tests,
including eight busy clocks and the ten-cycle ready-bus retirement
bound. Gowin placements 0/1/2 reached 68.372/70.439/70.439 MHz,
giving median 70.439 MHz with 4939 logic LUTs, 1045 registers, two DSPs
and four BSRAMs. The worst path was inside the final divider digit/sign
correction. The unchanged stalled CoreMark harness completed with all
canonical CRCs, required UART validation, no out-of-bounds accesses and
both timing markers in exactly 4,773,913 bracketed cycles. Combining
these measurements projects 147.550 iterations/sec, 11.25 percent above
132.63. A separate ALTOPS unit probe also passed the exact four formulas,
captured-input isolation, eight-clock schedule and held-result checks.
These are scratch measurements, not an orchestrator acceptance
or a completed formal/field-by-field trace-cosim gate.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure only the shared blocking DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU unit into raw
operand capture, combined first-digit/constant preparation, and seven
single-level parallel radix-16 digit clocks. Preserve exactly eight
busy clocks after launch and the existing result-transfer timing.
Raw capture removes magnitude negation from early decode launch;
one radix-16 digit replaces two serial full-width radix-4 digit stages.
These boundaries are one coherent divider structure: changing only
the launch boundary exposes the unchanged recurrence as the bottleneck.
Keep ordinary instruction latency, multiplication, fetch policy,
forwarding and all EX start/wait/accept equations unchanged.

At accepted start capture resolved raw a/b and operation/sign
metadata, with no arithmetic before those operand registers. The
existing quotient/divisor storage may hold raw values until group zero,
then be overwritten with prepared ordinary state. In group zero,
compute unsigned magnitudes and the first four quotient bits using
the existing two narrow radix-4 steps. If divisor magnitude is at
least 16, select quotient nibble zero and the top dividend-magnitude
nibble as remainder. Otherwise the narrow arithmetic selects both
two-bit digits. D=0 must select nibble 15 and retain the prefix.
Register quotient={magnitude_a[27:0],nibble}, zero-extended first
remainder, and divisor magnitude. Avoid a 32-bit carry chain before
the narrow first trial: for negative raw a compute its top magnitude
nibble as ~raw_a[31:28] + (raw_a[27:0]==0), modulo 16.
Detect D>=16 directly from raw b: for a negative signed operand it is
!(&raw_b[31:4]) || raw_b[3:0]==0; otherwise it is |raw_b[31:4].

Prepare and register all divisor multiples M[k]=k*abs(b), k=1..15,
at explicitly unsigned 36-bit width in this same first busy clock.
Do not put a conditional magnitude adder followed by multiple
adders in series. Let neg_b be the captured signed-negative flag and
V=zero_extend_36(raw_b XOR {32{neg_b}}), so abs(b)=V+neg_b.
Compute each odd multiple directly from V using carry-save compression
and one final carry-propagate sum. Define CSA3(x,y,z)=(x XOR y XOR z)
+ (((x&y)|(x&z)|(y&z))<<1), at 36 bits. For four terms, compress
three into sum/carry, compress those with the fourth, then add once.
Use M1=zero_extend_36(abs(b)), M3=CSA3(V<<1,V,neg_b?3:0),
M5=CSA3(V<<2,V,neg_b?5:0), M7=CSA3(V<<3,~V,neg_b?8:1),
M9=CSA3(V<<3,V,neg_b?9:0),
M11=CSA4(V<<3,V<<1,V,neg_b?11:0),
M13=CSA4(V<<3,V<<2,V,neg_b?13:0), and
M15=CSA3(V<<4,~V,neg_b?16:1). All complements, shifts, constants
and intermediate values are 36 bits; subtraction constructions
deliberately wrap modulo 2^36 to yield the exact nonnegative multiple.
For even k use M[k]=M[k/2]<<1. Reset all multiple registers, update
them only in group zero, and hold them during subsequent digit clocks.

In groups one through seven form the 36-bit trial
T={remainder_q,quotient_q[31:28]}. Evaluate all fifteen differences
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,M[k]} in parallel at 37-bit width. fits[k] is the
inverse borrow bit and fits[0]=1. Select k=15 with fits[15], and
k=0..14 with fits[k] && !fits[k+1]. Ordered nonnegative multiples
make these masks mutually exclusive; for D=0 they select k=15.
Select residual and four-bit digit with balanced masked ORs,
without a fifteen-level priority chain. k=0 selects T itself.
Keep full subtract widths until selection, then register the 32-bit
residual and quotient_next={quotient_q[27:0],digit}. Preserve the
existing final quotient/remainder selection and signed correction
when registering group seven's completed result, without another state.

Preserve signed truncation toward zero, the dividend's remainder sign,
non-negated all-ones DIV-by-zero quotient, REM-by-zero original dividend,
INT_MIN/-1 wraparound, unsigned maxima and x0. Live operand/op changes
after start must not affect captured work. Maintain progress behind
older stalled memory operations, stable completion until accepted,
reset cancellation, consecutive accept/start capability and exactly-once
result transfer, retirement and memory effects. Keep RVFI operand values
raw and architectural, with current instruction metadata ownership.

In RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, capture raw operands and operation at start,
evaluate the four unchanged subtraction/XOR formulas during group zero,
and return them on the identical eighth busy clock. Keep nret=1 and
every external IO/RVFI port, legality/trap check, retirement-order rule
and fixed formal liveness depth. Preserve early launch after taken
control transfers and dependent loads and the at-most-ten-cycle
ready-bus retirement gap; changing latency is not part of this proposal.

With unchanged CoreMark cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax above
approximately 66.231 MHz and fitness above 138.731 iterations/sec.
Expect eleven percent higher fitness with medium confidence. Main risks
are routing fifteen subtractors, first-group constant preparation and
final sign correction. Use real arithmetic and pipeline tests plus the
unchanged formal, trace cosim, CoreMark CRC/marker/UART and median Gowin
evaluation. Scratch artifacts are evidence only and must not become
build dependencies; recreate all logic in the permitted RTL files.

title: Folded-PC agree prediction with timing-isolated training
motivation:
The champion retires the canonical CoreMark run in 4,773,913 cycles
at 63.318 MHz, scoring 132.63 iter/sec. LESSONS.md is absent. All five
earlier predictor attempts passed correctness but lost their rounds;
the last 32-entry bimodal predictor took 4,485,269 cycles at 58.887 MHz.
Predictor recovery and routing costs consumed its throughput gain.
The new champion captures fully forwarded architectural operands in
ID/EX, removing the old EX operand/ALU feedback arrangement. Preserve
that timing boundary when integrating a small, more accurate predictor.

A fresh read-only run of the canonical 2K, -O3 reference program counted
529,588 conditional branches, 294,425 taken branches, 49,367 direct
JALs and 13,735 JALRs between markers, without traps or out-of-bounds
accesses. An immediate-training trace model gave 55,558 conditional
misses for the previous 32-entry PC-indexed bimodal organization,
versus 41,188 for 64 two-bit agreement counters indexed by
PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8], using the branch displacement sign as static
direction bias. Replaying counter updates delayed by two, three and
four architectural instruction events retained those same 41,188
misses. Agreement learning reduces destructive interference between
oppositely biased branches sharing an entry. These are trace estimates,
not RTL, random-stall or Gowin measurements.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact folded-PC agree predictor: 64 two-bit saturating
counters indexed by fetch PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8]. Each counter predicts
whether a conditional branch agrees with its static backward-taken,
forward-not-taken bias, rather than predicting absolute taken direction.
Reset counters to weakly agree (10). For a positively validated BRANCH
encoding, define bias_taken = instruction[31] and predicted_taken =
counter_MSB ? bias_taken : !bias_taken. Train with agreement =
resolved_taken == instruction[31]. Direct legal JAL is always predicted
to its immediate target; JALR stays sequential. Use one asynchronous
counter-MSB lookup, explicit clocked counter bits, no live EX bypass,
and no speculative history, target table, return stack or new stage.
This is solely a predictor hypothesis; keep all arithmetic, forwarding
and pipeline timing boundaries of the current champion intact.

Derive speculative B/J targets from raw fetched instruction bits,
sharing one short word-address adder. Accept source PCs only when
PC[31:20]==0 and PC[1:0]==0. Require displacement bit 1 zero. Form
target_word modulo 2^19 as {1'b0, PC[19:2]} plus the signed B/J
displacement divided by four, sign-extended to 19 bits. Require
target_word[18]==0; reconstruct {12'b0,target_word[17:0],2'b00}.
The admitted source and RV32 J displacement bounds make that high-bit
check reject negative and >=1-MiB sums without an unsafe modular alias.
A standalone mathematical check exhausted all 524,288 aligned JAL
word displacements at six source PCs spanning RAM boundaries and
the midpoint, passing 3,145,728 target admission/reconstruction cases.
Otherwise fall back to full-width PC+4 and leave the architectural
target and misalignment handling in EX authoritative. Validate legal
conditional funct3 values explicitly; reserved encodings never predict.

Carry a single predicted_transfer bit through if_id_t and id_ex_t,
captured, held and flushed with the instruction. The prediction always
uses that instruction's exact direct immediate target, so EX recovery
is actual_transfer XOR predicted_transfer rather than a wide next-PC
equality comparison. Derive actual_transfer from the existing branch
condition/jump controls, suppressed by the existing misalignment fault.
On a mismatch recover to the architectural target when transferring,
or the resolving instruction's own PC+4 on fall-through. Correct
predictions retain the fetched successor. Keep resolved pc_next,
link results, architectural operands and trap suppression for RVFI.

Prediction changes PC only on actual fetch acceptance. Hold PC and
instruction association during imem, load-use, dmem and arithmetic
waits. An advancing EX correction overrides fetch holds, including
imemReady=0. A branch held behind an older stalled memory operation
cannot redirect or retrain until EX advances. Qualify training with
valid, legal, nontrapping conditional EX acceptance exactly once.

Register one training transaction containing valid, the folded EX-PC
index and agreement outcome. On the following edge saturate the
current indexed counter, allowing consumption and a new enqueue on
the same edge. Clear pending valid when no branch is enqueued; consume
already queued training once even if the pipeline subsequently stalls.
Lookup/update collisions observe old state. Do not copy a stale fetch
counter snapshot into training or bypass the live resolved outcome
into lookup. This limits comparator fanout to a small update register.

Keep recovery off the early-divider operand and launch preparation
paths. Continue decoding raw instruction bits during flush. Supply
imem-ready raw decode eligibility independently of recovery and require
registered empty EX, validated DIV/REM, ready MEM and available units
for early launch. A correcting control instruction occupies EX, so
the mandatory empty-EX guard prevents a wrong-path early divide.
Choose raw decode versus EX operands only by registered EX occupancy.
Preserve divider latency, result acceptance, ready-bus liveness bounds
and the champion's captured alu_a/alu_b and rs1_val/rs2_val paths.

The trace model saves 302,604 one-cycle corrections, projecting
4,471,309 cycles and about 141.61 iter/sec at 63.318 MHz, a 6.8 percent
gain. More than 4.6 percent above 132.63 requires over 138.73098
iter/sec, or about 62.03 MHz at that projected cycle count. Delayed
training, bus-stall phase and placed routing require evaluation; there
is only about two percent clock margin. Preserve nret=1, every IO/RVFI
field, decoder legality, arithmetic and all formal, cosim, CRC, bounds,
MMIO-marker, UART and Gowin evaluation checks unchanged.

clocks: group zero consumes four more bits while preparing registered
divisor multiples; groups one through six consume one radix-16 digit
each. Thus 4+4+6*4=32 bits are consumed without a preparation clock.
Losing early launch costs one clock after a control transfer or load-use
bubble; folding the initial nibble into launch saves one busy clock.
Preserve the unchanged ten-cycle ready-bus retirement-gap bound.

On launch form unsigned magnitudes A and D and capture the existing
quotient/remainder signs, suppressing quotient negation for b=0.
Keep the original raw RVFI operands in EX metadata. Compute A's top
magnitude nibble directly: a[31:28] when nonnegative, otherwise
~a[31:28]+(a[27:0]==0), modulo 16. Compute D's low nibble with four-bit
conditional negation. Detect D>=16 directly from raw b: |b[31:4] when
nonnegative, otherwise !(&b[31:4]) || b[3:0]==0. For D>=16, digit=0
and residual=A's top nibble. For D<16, use a combinational constant
256-entry eight-bit table indexed by {top_A_nibble,low_D_nibble}.
Entry {P,d} is {P%d,P/d}; d=0 gives {P,4'hf}. Generate its 2048 literal
bits at implementation time, or equivalent constant case entries.
This table must have no runtime division or external initialization
dependency. Capture quotient_q={A[27:0],digit},
remainder_q={28'b0,residual}, divisor_q=D and divisor_3x_q=3*D.
Full A normalization runs in parallel. Do not replace the constant
lookup with two serial subtract/select stages: prototype timing showed
that those stages limit the registered launch path.

Prepare launch 3D with one carry-save compression and one 34-bit
carry-propagate sum, avoiding normalization followed by another wide
adder. Let n=signed_op && b[31], V={2'b0,b XOR {32{n}}};
compress V<<1, V and n?34'd3:34'd0 into sum/carry, then add them.
Explicit 34-bit widths preserve all unsigned and signed magnitudes.

During busy group zero the consumed prefix is at most 255. D>=256
appends digit zero and keeps {remainder_q[3:0],quotient_q[31:28]} as
the eight-bit residual. Otherwise consume two radix-4 digits with
ten-bit trial/divisor multiples, eleven-bit parallel borrow-producing
subtractions and eight-bit residuals. D/2D use divisor_q[7:0]; 3D uses
divisor_3x_q[9:0], exact when D<256. D=0 appends four ones and retains
the prefix. Capture the resulting nibble and zero-extended residual.

On that same group-zero edge register unsigned 36-bit M[k]=k*D for
k=1..15. Use M1=zero_extend(D), M3=zero_extend(divisor_3x_q),
M5=D+(D<<2), M7=(D<<3)-D, M9=D+(D<<3),
M11=CSA3(D,D<<1,D<<3), M13=CSA3(D,D<<2,D<<3), M15=(D<<4)-D;
even multiples are shifts of their half-index multiple. Widen before
shifting. CSA3 uses XOR sum, shifted majority carry and one final
addition. Reset the registers and update only in group zero.

For groups one through six form 36-bit T={remainder_q,quotient_q[31:28]}.
Compute fifteen 37-bit differences {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,M[k]} in parallel.
fits[k]=inverse borrow, fits[0]=1. Select digit 15 with fits[15] and
digit k=0..14 with fits[k] && !fits[k+1]. Use balanced masked OR trees,
with digit zero selecting T. Preserve full widths until selection,
then register the 32-bit residual and append the quotient nibble.
Group six captures the selected quotient/remainder magnitude in
result_magnitude_q. Preserve the champion's sign correction AFTER
this register; do not append a negate to the recurring trial path.

Preserve all exact ALTOPS formulas, capturing their substituted result
on launch and returning it after the same seven busy clocks as real
arithmetic. Preserve signed truncation, dividend-signed remainder,
divide-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, unsigned high-bit operands and x0.
Maintain pending-result/sign stability, reset cancellation, accept/
start overlap, independently held older memory requests and exactly-once
launch, result transfer, stores and retirement. Divider waits hold
fetch/ID/EX while older stages drain. Release ID/EX on result transfer
and retain completed-result forwarding. Keep nret=1, every IO/RVFI
field, decoder defaults, traps, bounds and all evaluation checks.

A scratch prototype of this organization passed all real divider and
pipeline cocotb cases, including the unchanged ten-cycle retirement
bound, plus additional first-byte/divisor-boundary differential cases.
Source-selection assertions now require registered EX launch; all
architectural operand, arithmetic, trap, order and side-effect checks
were retained. Gowin options 0/1/2 measured 80.987/81.007/81.007 MHz,
median 81.007 MHz, with 4649 logic cells, 1073 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs,
four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The worst option-zero path is now the ordinary
ALU-to-ID/EX recurrence, 17.642 ns. The final prototype also passed
full selftest trace cosim with and without both bus stalls. Canonical
2K CoreMark passed every CRC, the validation literal, both markers and
the no-OOB check, retaining exactly 4,773,913 bracketed cycles for ten
iterations under both stall generators. ALTOPS Verilator lint passed.
Full formal remains an implementation
gate and is not claimed here. Scratch files are evidence only and must
not become implementation build dependencies.

At unchanged champion cycles this median projects 169.69 iter/sec,
about 10.1 percent above 154.12; acceptance requires more than 161.21
iter/sec, approximately 76.96 MHz at those cycles. Expect ten percent
higher fitness with medium confidence. Risks are parallel-trial routing,
constant-table inference, signed launch corners and formal progress.

title: Agree prediction with registered direct recovery targets
motivation:
The current champion scores 154.12 iter/sec at 73.574 MHz and needs
4,773,913 cycles for the canonical ten-iteration CoreMark run.
LESSONS.md is absent. Six previous predictor experiments passed
correctness but lost their tournament rounds: recurring control
bubbles were removed, while their clock rates failed to beat the
arithmetic improvements competing in those rounds. The last agree
predictor needed 4,471,643 cycles, but ran on the previous divider.
The current champion's reported path still crosses EX, IF and early
divider launch. Adding prediction without shortening that recovery
path leaves only about two percent clock margin for acceptance.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact direct-control predictor whose recovery targets are
prepared before the existing ID/EX register. Use 64 two-bit agree
counters indexed by PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8], reset to weak agreement (10).
For positively validated conditional branches, use instruction[31]
as backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias, selecting that bias when
the counter MSB predicts agreement and its inverse otherwise.
Predict legal JAL unconditionally; keep JALR sequential. This is a
predictor-only change, preserving the current arithmetic units,
forwarded-operand capture, retirement width and pipeline stages.

Compute the exact full-width PC+B/J-immediate target and PC+4 from
the raw fetch PC/instruction before ID/EX. Share the direct-target
calculation between the fetch next-PC choice and the target carried
with that instruction; do not recompute the direct branch/JAL target
from registered PC and immediate in EX. Capture direct_target,
fallthrough_pc and one predicted_transfer bit in ID/EX, holding and
flushing them with the complete instruction. These are prepared
recovery addresses, not a cached target table. Keep full RV32 modular
target arithmetic; never substitute a truncated or range-clamped
speculative address for the architectural target. Admit speculative
transfers only for aligned source and target PCs inside instruction
RAM [0x00000000, 0x00100000). Otherwise predict sequentially and let
normal EX resolution retain its architectural trap/target behavior.

Resolve conditional direction from the existing captured architectural
operands. Select the already registered direct_target or fallthrough_pc
for direct-control recovery, actual RVFI pc_next and JAL link writes.
Keep the existing rs1+immediate JALR calculation and bit-zero clearing.
Suppress actual transfers on the existing target-misalignment fault.
Since every prediction uses the current instruction's exact direct
target, recovery requires only actual_transfer XOR predicted_transfer,
qualified by valid EX advance. There is no wide predicted-next-PC
comparison, stale target recovery for arithmetic instructions or
branch-target adder after the resolving branch comparator. Correct
predictions preserve the fetched successor; a direction error recovers
to the appropriate registered address. Preserve link-write suppression
on traps and architectural PC reporting independently of prediction.

Lookup depends only on registered fetch PC and stored direction state;
do not add lookahead reads indexed by a combinational next PC. Register
one training transaction containing valid, folded EX-PC index and
resolved agreement, qualified by valid, legal, nontrapping conditional
EX acceptance. On the next edge saturate the current indexed counter.
Consume queued training once even during subsequent pipeline stalls,
allow simultaneous consumption and enqueue, and use old-state lookup
on read/write collisions. Do not bypass live EX outcomes to lookup or
restore a stale fetched counter snapshot. Reset pending validity.

Advance the fetch PC to a prediction only when the fetched instruction
is accepted. Hold PC and prediction association during imem, load-use,
dmem and arithmetic waits. An advancing EX correction overrides fetch
holds, including imemReady=0. A branch behind an older stalled memory
operation cannot correct or train repeatedly. Existing hazard flush
control receives accepted prediction corrections rather than every
taken control transfer.

Keep correction off the empty-EX early-divider launch enable as well
as its operands: provide raw decode eligibility from imemReady,
independently of correction/flush, with the mandatory registered
!ID/EX.valid guard, validated DIV/REM decode, ready MEM and available
arithmetic units. A correcting branch necessarily occupies EX, making
that empty-slot guard sufficient to prohibit wrong-path early launch.
Keep raw instruction bits visible on flush and choose decode versus EX
divider operands/opcode only by registered EX occupancy. Preserve the
champion's early-launch latency, divider result handshake and existing
ready-bus retirement-gap bound; introduce no predictor-controlled
arithmetic data mux or additional arithmetic state.

The prior agree result suggests approximately 6.8 percent throughput
improvement from fewer cycles alone. Reusing prepared target and
fall-through addresses at EX is intended to retain or improve Fmax by
breaking the late target-arithmetic/recovery/launch timing chain.
At 4,471,643 cycles, acceptance over 154.12 by more than 4.6 percent
requires greater than 72.087 MHz; the current 73.574 MHz would score
about 164.53 iter/sec. These are projections, not measurements of this
candidate. Protect every IO/RVFI field, nret=1, decoder legality,
arithmetic result and unchanged formal/cosim/CRC/marker/UART/bounds
check. Gowin median Fmax and measured bracketed cycles decide fitness.

title: Predecode EX dispatch and forwarding eligibility into three ID/EX bits
motivation:
The champion scores 174.53 iterations/sec at median 83.321 MHz and
4,773,913 marker-bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
ID/EX ctrl.alu_op[4] and crosses EX into the timed memory circuit.
A fresh unchanged vendor build reproduced placement-zero Fmax
85.334 MHz and the same 17.013 ns operation-control path. EX repeatedly
classifies the binary operation and combines instruction properties
to authorize normal-result forwarding. Those controls participate in
the EX-result-to-decode recurrence. LESSONS.md is absent; the prior
micro_opt entries address divider arithmetic and forwarding selection,
rather than predecoding this current EX instruction's dispatch and
normal-forwarding eligibility at its existing admission boundary.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming three instruction-only predicates into the existing ID/EX
register should shorten EX control and forwarding paths while preserving
every instruction's latency. Add logic fast_write, mul_class, div_class
to id_ex_t, in that order immediately after alu_b and before imm.
This is a single local predecode optimization with three added control
flip-flops; retain the current five-bit ALU opcode, ALU result mux,
arithmetic datapaths, pipeline boundaries and execution schedules.

In id_stage's decoded next-state bundle, calculate mul_class from the
existing decoded ALU operation equal to MUL, MULH, MULHU or MULHSU.
Calculate div_class from operation equal to DIV, DIVU, REM or REMU.
Compute fast_write = dec_reg_write && !dec_mem_read && !dec_is_illegal
&& !decoded.mul_class && !decoded.div_class. These predicates describe
the candidate instruction before capture, independently of bus ready,
redirect, launch and arithmetic-unit occupancy. Capture them with its
final architectural operands, controls and metadata using the unchanged
authoritative ID/EX reset/flush/hold/invalid-bubble logic. An invalid
bubble remains entirely zero; all three flags hold with a held instruction.

In ex_stage replace operation equality networks with exactly
is_mul = in.valid && in.mul_class and
is_div = in.valid && in.div_class. Replace only the initial normal-result
forwarding qualification with
forward_wen = in.valid && in.fast_write && !misalign_fault.
Keep dynamic branch/JAL/JALR misalignment suppression in EX. Retain the
existing subsequent mul_valid/div_valid overrides, their priority,
destination selection and completed-result data. Keep every original
launch, busy, pending-result, memory-hold, acceptance, drain-bubble and
redirect guard unchanged. Preserve the binary opcode connection to
alu, mul_unit and div_unit, including exact ALTOPS behavior. No source
tag comparison or forwarding-data selection is moved across a cycle.

For every valid instruction, the new normal-forwarding expression is
algebraically identical to the old expression: its !is_mul/!is_div terms
reduce to the captured class exclusions when in.valid is true. Both
expressions are false for invalid work. Keeping the instruction-only
part in decode removes repeated opcode and writeback-property decoding
after the EX operand register; misalignment and completed-result choices
retain their actual-cycle qualification. Decoder legality remains the
original default-illegal decoder; the new flags cannot authorize work
independently of validity or change trap or retirement behavior.

A scratch prototype of precisely these three added flags and three
EX expression replacements passed the entire existing pipeline cocotb
suite, strict Verilator lint, and full selftest RVFI trace cosim both

passed the unchanged evaluator's CRC/UART/marker/bounds validation and
retained exactly 4,773,913 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. Gowin
placement options 0/1/2 measured 81.571/91.790/91.790 MHz: median
91.790 MHz, 4594 logic cells and 1076 registers, versus champion 4592
and 1073, with unchanged 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The
median-placement worst path is now ALU-to-memory at 16.189 ns.
These are prototype measurements, not an orchestrator acceptance result.
Full formal remains an implementation gate and is not claimed here.
Scratch sources and artifacts are evidence only, never build dependencies.

sensitivity. Acceptance requires more than 182.558 iterations/sec,
approximately 87.154 MHz at unchanged cycles. Require the unchanged
formal, arithmetic, trace cosim, canonical CoreMark validation and
median vendor fitness gates. Keep nret=1, every external memory/RVFI
port, captured operands, traps, strict order, bounded progress, arbitrary
bus backpressure and all evaluation invariants without modification.

title: Separate EX/MEM payload capture from arithmetic bubble control
motivation:
The champion scores 174.53 iter/sec at median 83.321 MHz with
4,773,913 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent.
Structural history favors registered execution boundaries: isolated
multiplication, captured decode operands, and registered-only divider
dispatch won their rounds. Gowin reproduces the champion's 17.013 ns
worst path from ID/EX ALU-operation control to the FPGA data RAM.
EX currently handles a multiply/divide wait by zeroing the entire
EX/MEM bundle, putting instruction classification and busy control into
the common wide data-register input mux. A bubble needs to disable
retirement, forwarding and memory effects; it does not need to select
zero separately for every operand, result and metadata bit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the existing EX/MEM register into independent payload and
occupancy/control updates. Preserve its physical pipeline boundary,
ordinary instruction latency and all existing execution units. Keep
reset clearing the complete register and a data-memory stall holding
the complete register. Keep completed multiply and divide acceptance
selecting their saved metadata and registered results exactly as now.

On every other unstalled edge capture the existing normal EX payload:
pc, ordinary ALU or jump-link result, raw store data, destination and
source tags, architectural source values, resolved next PC, branch
metadata and instruction. Do this even while a blocking arithmetic
operation is waiting. Replace the whole-bundle zero assignment for
mul_wait || is_div || div_busy with clearing ONLY reg_q.ctrl and
reg_q.valid on those edges. Concretely, retain the normal payload
assignment arm and assign ctrl = waiting ? '0 : ctrl_with_trap,
valid = in.valid && !waiting, where waiting is the existing exact
mul_wait || is_div || div_busy expression. A waiting payload is
architecturally inactive. Do not convert this into holding the older
EX/MEM entry: the older ready instruction must advance once and then
leave an invalid entry, preventing an older store from being reissued.

Preserve the original ordering of reset, data hold, multiply acceptance,
divide acceptance and ordinary payload capture. Keep start, busy,
result-valid, result-accept, divider_wait, forwarding and redirect
equations unchanged. On unready data buses preserve the whole older
request; arithmetic may progress independently and pending completion
stays stable until accepted. Keep MEM/WB valid clearing on data stalls
and every side-effect gate. Retain fully zeroed ID/EX bubbles and its
existing flush/hold priority; this proposal changes only the EX/MEM
payload update boundary. There is no additional stage or cycle.

Keep nret=1 and every IO/RVFI field, decoder-default legality, traps,
memory bounds, architectural operand reporting, exactly-once effects,
retirement order and the ten-cycle ready-bus progress bound. Preserve
all real multiplier/divider arithmetic, their latencies and exact
ALTOPS branches. Keep every existing test assertion; in particular,
the invalid-ID/EX whole-zero check remains valid and unchanged. Add
focused checks that an arithmetic-wait EX/MEM entry has zero control
and valid, cannot issue memory operations or retire, and clears an
older ready store exactly once while holding an unready one.

A scratch prototype of this exact change passed all 25 existing
pipeline cocotb tests unchanged, including dependency, stall, trap,
exactly-once side-effect and ready-bus progress checks. It also passed
full selftest trace cosim with ready buses and with both random bus

title: Agree prediction behind the registered arithmetic boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 174.53 iter/sec at 83.321 MHz and takes 4,773,913
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Seven earlier
predictor attempts passed correctness but lost their rounds. The last
folded-PC agree predictor reduced the same workload to 4,471,643 cycles,
yet its 75.685 MHz worst path traversed EX, predictor recovery and early
divider launch. The new champion launches arithmetic exclusively from
registered ID/EX operands and has removed that recovery-to-launch path.

early decode dispatch. The measured cycle reduction is worth about
6.76 percent throughput at constant Fmax; retaining above 81.634 MHz would be
sufficient to exceed the champion by the required 4.6 percent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one small direct-control agree predictor to the current champion,
preserving its registered-only multiplier/divider dispatch. Use 64
two-bit saturating agreement counters indexed by PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8],
reset to weak agreement (10). For positively validated conditional
branches, instruction[31] supplies backward-taken/forward-not-taken
bias; predict the bias when the counter MSB is one, its inverse when
zero. Predict direct JAL taken and JALR sequential. There is no target
cache, global history, return stack, extra pipeline stage or additional
memory speculation. This reuses the prior measured agree organization
at the champion's newly established arithmetic timing boundary.

Prepare exact full-width modular PC+B/J-immediate and PC+4 addresses
before the existing ID/EX register. Share the direct-target value
between fetch prediction and the recovery address captured with its
instruction. Carry direct_target, fallthrough_pc and predicted_transfer
in IF/ID and ID/EX; hold and clear them with the instruction. EX uses
registered direct/fall-through targets instead of recomputing branch
and JAL addresses. Preserve the existing full-width rs1+imm calculation
and bit-zero clearing for JALR, target-misalignment traps, suppressed
link writes on traps, and exact architectural RVFI pc_next values.
Speculate a direct transfer only for aligned source and target PCs
inside [0x00000000, 0x00100000). Otherwise predict sequentially and
retain the full architectural target for EX resolution and trapping;
do not truncate or clamp architectural addresses.

Because admitted direct targets come from the current instruction,
recovery needs actual_transfer XOR predicted_transfer, rather than
a wide predicted-next-PC comparator. Define actual_transfer as a
legal, nontrapping taken branch or jump, including sequentially
predicted JALR. Qualify correction with valid EX acceptance (!stall).
Correct predictions preserve the fetched successor. On a mismatch,
choose the already registered target or fall-through PC, with the
existing JALR result where applicable, and flush the younger decode.
Prediction advances fetch only when the instruction is admitted:
imem ready, no load-use, dmem or arithmetic hold, and no correction.
Accepted correction overrides fetch holds including imemReady=0.
A branch held behind an older memory operation neither corrects nor
trains repeatedly. Preserve raw instruction/decode visibility during
flush, operand forwarding, and existing invalid-entry zeroing.

Give direction lookup exactly one read of stored table state indexed
only by the registered fetch PC. Enqueue one accepted legal nontrapping
conditional-branch training event containing folded index and resolved
agreement, then consume it on the following edge. Saturate the current
indexed counter, never a stale prediction snapshot. Permit simultaneous
consume/enqueue and consume each event exactly once independently of

their arithmetic, latency, or result handshakes. Existing start/opcode/
operand selection must remain exclusively functions of registered
ID/EX occupancy and arithmetic-unit state. Predictor recovery and table
training must not gate those starts or select their operands. Preserve
the current EX/MEM hold and drain behavior, completed-result forwarding,
no wrong-path arithmetic or stores, and the existing liveness bound.

The prior 4,471,643-cycle result projects 186.33 iter/sec at the
champion's 83.321 MHz, a 6.76 percent gain. The acceptance requirement

headroom. These are projections from a previous implementation, not
measurements of this candidate; measured bracketed cycles and Gowin
median Fmax decide success. Preserve nret=1, every IO/RVFI port,
decoder legality, arithmetic and all unchanged formal, cosim, CoreMark

title: Capture complete fast-forwarding eligibility including jump alignment
motivation:
The champion scores 192.27 iterations/sec at median 91.790 MHz with
4,773,913 measured CoreMark cycles. The previous winning micro_opt
captured instruction classification and forwarding eligibility at ID/EX,
gaining 10.16 percent. A fresh unchanged Gowin build reproduces 91.790 MHz
and shows competing ALU-to-memory, EX-to-decode and divider paths.
No LESSONS.md exists. EX still puts dynamic misalign_fault qualification
after the captured fast_write flag. That qualification depends on branch
comparison and jump target calculation and feeds the decode operand masks.
Capturing the complete eligibility predicate should shorten this feedback
path without adding state or instruction cycles.

In id_stage add a two-bit combinational jump_target_low equal to

(dec_is_jalr ? jump_target_low[1] : |jump_target_low).

JAL requires both summed low bits zero. A two-bit sum exactly captures
the relevant bits of the existing 32-bit target calculation, including

suppress architectural writes exactly as before. This precomputed flag

captured into ID/EX and remain stable when older producers drain during

introduced. Keep the binary operation, arithmetic units and ALTOPS intact.

shared-shifter arithmetic mappings reduced Fmax, and removing only branch

title: Separate the registered memory-address lane from execute writeback
motivation:
The current champion scores 192.27 iterations/sec at 91.790 MHz with
4,773,913 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts
at ID/EX alu_a and passes through the integer ALU and execute selection
to the data-memory RAM. Every data-memory address currently comes from
EX/MEM alu_result, a shared register whose input also selects integer
results, jump links, multiplier completion, divider completion and
arithmetic-wait bubbles. These selections unnecessarily precede the
address of a load or store. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior structural attempts
successfully separated blocking arithmetic and registered operands, but
the last attempt merely changing EX/MEM bubble payload capture scored
188.93 and lost. A dedicated address lane removes a concrete shared
datapath dependency instead of relying on payload-control remapping.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

execute writeback result. Add a full-width mem_addr field to ex_mem_t,
driven by its own register update in ex_stage. Compute the effective
address directly as in.alu_a + in.alu_b, using the already registered,
fully forwarded ID/EX operands. For every legal LOAD/STORE those inputs
are precisely architectural rs1 and the sign-extended immediate. The
address register must capture this sum on every edge when !stall and
clear on reset. It holds on the existing data-memory stall. Give this
field one sequential driver separate from the existing EX/MEM payload
priority mux; exclude it from any whole-bundle assignment so there is
no multiply/divide-completion, jump-link, opcode-result, or wait-bubble
selection on its input. A named independent address register assigned
into the output bundle is an equivalent implementation. Do not gate
address updates with live mem_read/mem_write, launch, completion or
redirect signals. Addresses in inactive entries may carry this harmless
speculative sum, while the existing valid/control gates authorize all
actual requests. Arithmetic units continue to progress independently.

Route every real memory address consumer in mem_stage to the new field:
io_dmemAddr, byte-lane position, load extraction, alignment checks and
word-aligned RVFI mem_addr. Preserve exact 32-bit modular addition and
every byte/halfword/word behavior, signed load, store replication and
misalignment trap. Keep the existing alu_result field and its selection
for ordinary register writeback and forwarding. A load's integer-ALU
address result may remain in that field, but memory requests no longer
depend on it. Do not pre-align, truncate, clamp or cache bus addresses.

Keep the original EX/MEM reset, data hold, completed MUL acceptance,
completed DIV acceptance, wait-bubble and normal-payload behavior for
every other field, including zero control and valid during arithmetic
waits. A waiting entry may have a nonzero dedicated address but cannot
request memory or retire. Preserve pending-result metadata, actual RVFI
operands, all result forwarding and load-use interlocks. The held older
LOAD/STORE retains its address, data and enables until ready. On the
edge it advances, the independently captured address belongs to the
next normal EX entry; an arithmetic completion or bubble has no memory
controls. Older stores drain exactly once. Redirects flush younger work
using the unchanged rules; a wrong-path address without an enable has
no side effect. Reset cancels all valid work and clears the address.

This is one structural separation of address generation from execute
writeback, with no extra pipeline stage, new predictor, cache, changed
arithmetic algorithm or changed instruction latency. Preserve nret=1,
all external IO/RVFI ports, decoder default-illegal discipline, exact
real RV32M and ALTOPS behavior, strict retirement order, forward progress,
memory bounds and every unchanged evaluation check. Retain existing
tests and add directed association/hold checks for the separate address
lane through memory backpressure, arithmetic waits/completion, redirects,
consecutive memory operations, load-dependent addresses and traps.

At unchanged measured cycles the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold is

are duplication/routing of the address adder, synthesis sharing and
a different critical path becoming limiting. This candidate has not
been measured; require unchanged formal, real-arithmetic tests, full
trace cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/bounds validation and
median Gowin timing before claiming an improvement.

title: Isolate branch recovery from every decode operand capture dependency
motivation:
The champion scores 192.27 iterations/sec at median 91.790 MHz with
4,773,913 measured CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Recent
micro_opt and structural candidates expose a 38-cell path from
ID/EX rs2[0] through branch resolution and redirect back into ID/EX
alu_b. Although IF exposes raw instruction bits, ID still zeroes its
entire packed register on flush or invalid fetch. Thus redirect
controls every wide operand's data mux. Fetch-valid qualification of
load-use detection also feeds redirect into the operand hold enable.
The r9 predictor experiment improved its median clock from 84.648
to 89.562 MHz after isolating these dependencies. Applying that local
isolation without prediction avoids the lookup and target circuitry.
The r9s0 micro_opt removed dynamic fault qualification from EX
forwarding alone, but left flush feedback intact and regressed to
85.904 MHz. The proposed single angle is complete isolation of branch
recovery from decode operand capture, including its forwarding gate.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate payload capture from bubble control inside the existing
ID/EX register, and remove redirect from its load-use hold predicate.
This is one control/data-path micro-optimization: retain all pipeline
boundaries, architectural latencies, fetch policy, execution units,
forwarding data priority and EX/MEM storage. Add no predictor or state.

Reset continues to clear the entire ID/EX register. On every nonreset
unstalled edge, capture decoded pc, rs1_val, rs2_val, alu_a, alu_b,
imm, rd, rs1_addr, rs2_addr and instr independently of flush and
in.valid. On a stall hold these payload fields. Neither redirect,
flush nor fetch acceptance may select zero at these payload D inputs
or qualify their capture enable. Keep operands prepared from the
existing resolved forwarding values and existing decode muxes.

Update occupancy and side-effect controls independently. Clear valid,
ctrl, fast_write, mul_class and div_class on flush, even when stall
is asserted, preserving the existing flush-over-hold load-use bubble
priority. When not flushed and unstalled, capture these fields from
decoded only if in.valid; otherwise clear them all. When stalled
without flush, hold them. An invalid bubble may contain discarded raw
payload but must have zero control and dispatch flags. Clearing only
valid is insufficient: keep all inactive forwarding, register-write,
memory and arithmetic-launch qualifications harmless. Retain the
existing zeroing of EX/MEM arithmetic-wait entries and every MEM/WB
backpressure rule; this proposal does not change those registers.

At core's hazard-unit connection, supply io_imemReady as the raw
fetch-eligibility input to load-use detection instead of if_id_w.valid,
which includes redirect suppression. Retain the same source/destination
comparisons, EX-load validity, x0 exclusion and every stall/flush
equation. For every reachable instruction, a redirecting BRANCH/JAL/
JALR cannot simultaneously be an EX load, and a load cannot redirect.
Consequently the new interlock is cycle-equivalent whenever a load
can actually block fetch, but no redirect dependency remains on the
payload hold enable. Document and verify that mutual exclusion;
do not rely on synthesis inferring it from correlated signals.
Keep ordinary IF acceptance validity, redirect priority over fetch
holds and all instruction/data bus backpressure unchanged.

Complete the same isolation at EX forwarding: its normal permission
currently includes !misalign_fault, which depends on live conditional
branch comparison even though branches never write a destination.
Capture the complete normal eligibility in the existing fast_write
bit. In ID form jump_target_low =
(dec_is_jalr ? rs1_data[1:0] : in.pc[1:0]) + imm[1:0], modulo four,
using the final forwarded rs1 value. Define jump_fault_decoded =
dec_is_jump && (dec_is_jalr ? jump_target_low[1] : |jump_target_low).
JALR clears bit zero; the low two-bit sum includes its carry into bit
one. Add !jump_fault_decoded to the existing fast_write predicate.
In EX use in.valid && in.fast_write for only the initial normal
forward_wen. Preserve completed MUL/DIV overrides and their priority,
tags and data. Preserve full-width jump/branch target arithmetic,
misalign_fault, ctrl_with_trap, redirect suppression and pc_next.
Conditional branches cannot be fast writers, so their dynamic faults
need not gate normal forwarding. All other faults exclude forwarding
exactly through the captured jump predicate. This removes the remaining
live branch outcome from the decode operand data masks; neither this
forwarding change nor payload isolation alone cuts every dependency.

This removes a late branch-comparison result and its high fanout from
wide decode register data and enable paths. Preserve nret=1, all
external IO/RVFI fields, default-illegal decoding, branch and memory
traps, captured architectural operands, exact retirement order and
all existing progress and memory-safety requirements. Preserve exact
real RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic and their existing schedules. Raw
inactive payload must never forward, launch arithmetic, redirect,
issue memory traffic, write a register or retire.

A fresh unchanged scratch Gowin build reproduces 91.790 MHz. Explicit
carry-prefix arithmetic and flatter result-selection scratch variants
reduced placement-one Fmax, so they are excluded from this proposal.
Payload-only isolation also reduced placement-one Fmax to 86.374 MHz
and exposed the remaining EX-to-forwarding feedback. The complete
isolation prototype is being checked independently. At
unchanged CoreMark cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax above
approximately 96.012 MHz and fitness above 201.114 iterations/sec.
Estimate ten percent with low confidence; branch-to-PC, ALU-to-memory
and divider paths can still dominate. These are projections, not an
accepted measurement. Require unchanged formal, arithmetic, full
trace cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/bounds checks,
followed by median vendor timing. Scratch files are evidence only.

title: Decouple instruction fetch with a four-entry fall-through queue
motivation:
The champion scores 192.27 iter/sec at 91.79 MHz and needs 4,773,913
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its combinational IF/ID view couples
the fetch PC to every load-use, data-memory and arithmetic hold. During
those holds an otherwise ready instruction bus does no useful work;
after execution resumes, an unready instruction bus immediately inserts
another bubble. With roughly 22 percent independent stalls on each bus,
buffering instructions obtained during backend holds can reduce these
serial penalties. Prior structural address-lane and EX/MEM payload
changes did not improve the champion, and no LESSONS.md exists. Scratch
payload-control and faster-multiplier alternatives in this proposal
session also lost too much Gowin Fmax. Decoupling fetch attacks measured
cycle cost without extending the arithmetic datapaths.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the globally held fetch view with an autonomous sequential
fetch producer and a four-entry, fall-through instruction FIFO. Keep
the existing single-issue ID/EX, EX/MEM and MEM/WB boundaries, operand
forwarding and blocking arithmetic units. This is one structural
separation of frontend production from backend consumption; the FIFO
is neither a cache nor a predictor and contains only fetched instruction
words and their associated full-width PCs.

When the FIFO is empty, present the current raw bus instruction and
producer PC directly to decode. Accept it only when io_imemReady and
decode acceptance are both true. Consume directly without enqueueing
and advance the producer PC by four on that edge. This empty bypass is
essential: a compulsory registered IF/ID stage would add a bubble to
every taken control transfer and could erase the gain. Keep raw fetch
data visible for combinational decode independently of acceptance.

When decode is held and the instruction bus is ready, enqueue the
current producer instruction/PC if there is capacity, advancing the
producer PC even though ID/EX cannot advance. When the FIFO is nonempty,
decode sees its oldest instruction and PC and can accept that head
even with io_imemReady=0. Independently fetch/enqueue the producer word
on a ready bus whenever space exists, including space freed by a
simultaneous dequeue. The producer PC advances exactly once for each
accepted bus word, whether directly consumed or enqueued. Never enqueue
an unready response, lose a full-queue word, or enqueue the same response
twice. Full FIFO plus no dequeue holds the producer PC. A stopped bus
holds the producer address while buffered decode can continue.

Prefer a shallow four-word shift FIFO with a fixed registered head and
a single empty/head bypass mux, rather than an asynchronous indexed RAM
read or a late backend-ready mux on every instruction bit. Store PCs
explicitly, or use a registered head PC whose sequential increments
are proved to remain associated with the stored words; do not derive
the head PC through a full-width subtractor on the decode path. Use
registered occupancy and queue state to select the raw/head payload.
Redirect, flush, io_imemReady and arithmetic completion must qualify
acceptance/control rather than select or zero wide decode payloads.
Reset queue control and payload deterministically.

An accepted EX redirect has highest priority: clear all queued younger
words, suppress direct consumption/enqueue/dequeue on that edge and
load the producer PC with the exact existing redirect target. Flush the
currently exposed younger decode instruction with the existing rules.
Redirect must override an unready bus, a full queue and fetch holds;
a branch behind an older unready memory request must still wait for
the existing EX advance before redirecting. Do not bypass-fetch a new
target on the redirect edge. The next cycle uses the empty FIFO bypass,
preserving current ready-bus branch/JAL/JALR timing and all misalignment
trap/link-write behavior. Use full 32-bit modular PCs and existing bus
addresses; introduce no address truncation, clamping or safe-target
substitution. Wrong-path prefetched words never reach side effects.

Separate hazard meanings explicitly. Backend holds continue to govern
ID/EX, load-use bubble injection, EX/MEM and MEM/WB exactly as today,
but do not prohibit producer prefetch. Instruction availability for
the hazard unit becomes head_valid || io_imemReady; its lack suppresses
decode acceptance only when no buffered head exists. Load-use checks
use the exposed consumer instruction's source tags, never the producer
io_imemData tags. Keep the valid EX-load and nonzero-rd comparisons.
A load-use bubble retains the queue head while the producer may fill
spare entries. MUL/DIV waits likewise retain the oldest consumer and
permit bounded prefetch; older data requests and completed arithmetic
retain the existing hold/drain/accept protocol. Wire an explicit
consumer-accept handshake so a flush-over-hold load-use edge cannot
accidentally dequeue. Buffered acceptance is independent of instruction
bus readiness but still forbidden by every real backend hold.

Preserve nret=1 and every top-level bus/RVFI port, decoder default
illegality, traps, exact RV32M and ALTOPS behavior, architectural source
operands and PCs, strict retirement order, bounded memory accesses,
exactly-once stores and the unchanged formal liveness/progress checks.
Keep all arithmetic and architectural tests. Update only frontend
microarchitecture assertions that equate io_imemData with the consumed
instruction when a buffered head is present; check the selected raw/head
payload and PC explicitly instead of weakening those assertions.

This FIFO candidate is unmeasured. Project a nine percent fitness gain
with medium confidence from hiding instruction stalls after load-use,
dmem and arithmetic holds. At unchanged 91.79 MHz, acceptance requires
fewer than about 4,564,000 bracketed cycles, a reduction greater than
4.4 percent. More generally require median_Fmax_Hz * 10 / measured_cycles
greater than 201.11442 iter/sec. A five percent Fmax loss would require
about a 9.2 percent cycle reduction, so the added head/bypass mux and
occupancy fanout are material risks. Confirm the tradeoff with unchanged
formal, real-arithmetic suites, full-trace cosim, canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/marker/bounds checks and all three Gowin placement options.

title: Agree prediction with recovery address selected before branch resolution
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The current champion scores 192.27 iter/sec at
91.79 MHz over 4,773,913 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Prior folded-PC
agree prediction repeatedly reduced that workload to 4,471,643 cycles.
The r9s2 predictor passed formal and cosim and reached 200.29 iter/sec
at 89.562 MHz, missing the 201.11442 acceptance threshold narrowly.
Its 38-cell worst path went from registered rs2 through EX/predictor
recovery to the fetch PC. Registering direct targets and isolating
decode payload capture removed earlier timing problems, but selecting
the correction address with the live resolved outcome still puts a
wide address mux after the branch comparator. On a direction mismatch,
the correct direct successor is the opposite of the captured prediction;
its address can therefore be chosen before the branch resolves.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one 64-entry folded-PC agree predictor with a correction
address preselected before ID/EX. Retain the proven organization:
two-bit saturating counters indexed by PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8], reset to
weak agreement (10). A positively validated conditional branch uses
instruction[31] as backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias; the counter
MSB selects that bias or its inverse. Predict legal direct JAL taken,
keep JALR sequential, and use the current instruction's immediate for
direct targets. Use one old-state lookup and an exactly-once registered
training event, without live EX-update bypass or stale counter snapshots.

Compute full-width modular direct_target = PC+B/J-immediate and
fallthrough_pc = PC+4 before ID/EX. Admit speculative direct transfers
only for aligned source and target PCs inside [0x00000000, 0x00100000).
Otherwise set predicted_transfer=0 while retaining the full architectural
direct target. Carry direct_target, fallthrough_pc, predicted_transfer
and recovery_pc with the accepted instruction. Crucially prepare
recovery_pc = predicted_transfer ? fallthrough_pc : direct_target
BEFORE ID/EX, using the final admitted prediction, not the raw table bit.
Hold these fields with their instruction. The recovery address must
never be selected by the live branch_cond, actual_transfer, mismatch,
training outcome, or predictor update in EX.

EX computes the authoritative direction and existing misalignment
fault from captured operands and targets. Define actual_transfer as
a legal nontrapping taken branch or jump; redirect on valid EX advance
and (actual_transfer XOR predicted_transfer). For direct BRANCH/JAL
correction, drive redirect_target directly from registered recovery_pc.
If prediction was taken, a mismatch means fall-through; if prediction
was sequential, a mismatch means the architectural direct target.
Keep the separate architectural pc_next selection for RVFI/retirement.
Never reuse that outcome-selected pc_next bus as the fetch correction
address. An accepted correction controls only the final fetch-PC write
selection and validity kills, with no outcome-controlled 32-bit target
selection ahead of that final PC mux. Keep ordinary JALR correction
on its existing full-width rs1+imm target with bit zero cleared, selected
by registered is_jalr, and preserve its misalignment/link suppression.
Correct predictions preserve the successor and introduce no new stage
or recovery cycle. There is no BTB, global history, or return stack.

Retain the r9s2 integration needed to keep recovery off decode payload
data inputs and enables. On unstalled nonreset edges capture raw operand,
address, tag, instruction and prediction payloads independently of
flush/fetch validity; separately clear valid, ctrl, fast_write, mul_class
and div_class for bubbles or correction. Preserve flush-over-hold for
load-use bubble injection. Invalid payload cannot forward, redirect,
launch arithmetic, access memory or retire. Use raw imemReady eligibility
for load-use detection rather than correction-qualified fetch valid:
an EX load and an EX control correction are mutually exclusive, so this
preserves real interlocks while removing the correction-to-payload-enable

title: Complete narrow-operand MUL directly into its held result register
motivation: The champion scores 204.02 iterations/sec at 91.231 MHz over 4,471,643 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The micro_opt history contains divider carry/sign optimizations, dispatch predecode and forwarding qualification, but no operand-width specialization of multiplication. The current multiplier spends a launch edge capturing operands and two busy edges registering partial products and the final result, even for small operands. CoreMark's matrix routines multiply sign-extended 16-bit MATDAT values, so many general 32-bit MUL instructions have operands that fit one native FPGA multiplier. Scratch ALU carry/result-selection and divider selector changes have not improved the tested placement option; shortening common multiplication latency offers a direct cycles-per-iteration benefit instead of relying entirely on timing gains.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one operand-width fast path inside mul_unit for ALU_MUL only. Keep the existing general partial-product multiplier, all MULH/MULHU/MULHSU behavior and the core's pipeline boundaries and result handshake. This is a local arithmetic specialization, with no new instruction, issue policy, predictor, cache or benchmark-specific detection.

Recognize narrow_mul = (op == ALU_MUL) && ((a[31:16] == 0) || (&a[31:16])) && ((b[31:16] == 0) || (&b[31:16])). Each qualifying 32-bit operand represents an integer in [-65536,65535], exactly expressible as the signed 17-bit value {operand[31], operand[15:0]}. This includes both sign-extended signed halfwords and zero-extended unsigned halfwords, as well as negative values down to -65536. It does not require low bit 15 to equal bit 31. Compute a signed 17x17 product at an explicit 34-bit width and use its low 32 bits. Low-word multiplication is identical modulo 2^32 regardless of whether the original RV32 operands are interpreted as signed or unsigned. The guard must be evaluated from the final registered EX architectural operands presented at accepted launch, with no PC, memory address, CoreMark marker or program-content condition.

On an accepted narrow launch, capture narrow_product[31:0] directly into the existing result register, set result_valid=1 and busy=0, and skip both busy clocks. There must be no combinational narrow-product bypass into decode or EX/MEM: the fast result and its metadata are registered on the launch edge. Keep the general launch and both busy phases exactly for every nonqualifying MUL and every high-word multiplication. Preserve reset, capture priority for simultaneous result_accept and a new start, refusal of starts during busy or an unaccepted pending result, and stable result_valid/result until acceptance. Internal arithmetic completion remains independent of older dmem backpressure.

The existing ex_stage already captures mul_meta_q on mul_start and consumes a registered mul_valid only when MEM can advance. Use that protocol unchanged: metadata and fast result become available on the same edge; the following result-transfer edge releases the held instruction and forwards the exact result to younger decode. Preserve MUL-over-DIV completion priority and bubble/drain behavior, with no replay, duplicate register write or repeated store. Do not add early decode launch or an arithmetic path through the younger forwarding resolver.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, use the identical narrow predicate and completion schedule but capture the existing ALU_MUL launch_result formula on the fast edge; preserve all existing formulas and the slow ALTOPS schedule for other cases. The real 17x17 product belongs only in the real arithmetic branch. Implement explicit signed casts and widths so 0x0000ffff and 0xffff0000 represent +65535 and -65536 respectively.

This removes two multiplier wait clocks per qualifying MUL. The projected gain is eight percent with low confidence pending whole-core timing and measured fast-path incidence. At unchanged Fmax, clearing the 4.6 percent acceptance margin requires fewer than about 4,275,000 measured cycles; an Fmax change must be combined with the observed cycle count rather than assumed. The principal risks are the DSP-to-result launch path reducing Fmax, extra DSP/mux area perturbing placement, and insufficient narrow MUL frequency. Inspect Gowin mapping of the 17x17 product and use the median over all placement options. Keep only this fast path in the submitted implementation; scratch alternatives are not part of the hypothesis.

Preserve the nret=1 IO/RVFI contract, exact retirement order and operands, all trap/decoder rules, full RV32M results, memory bounds and unchanged evaluation contracts. Retain every existing arithmetic assertion. Update only latency and partial-product-state expectations to distinguish the exactly specified fast and slow paths. Check all sign combinations, eligibility boundaries, fallback cases, mixed high/low operations, input poisoning, pending-result backpressure, reset, and simultaneous accept/start. Run real multiplier tests, pipeline dependence/stall tests, unchanged formal and cosim gates, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/bounds checks, and median Gowin timing before accepting a gain.

title: Decouple predicted fetch with a two-entry instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 204.02 iterations/sec at 91.231 MHz over 4,471,643
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Fetch currently stops on backend
load-use, data-memory and M-extension holds, preventing overlap with
independent instruction-bus readiness. LESSONS.md is absent. The r10s1
four-entry fall-through queue gained 2.95 percent on a champion without
the current agree predictor and missed acceptance. A temporary queue
preserving the current prediction metadata passed stalled selftest
trace cosim and all canonical CoreMark CRC/marker/bounds checks,
reducing measured cycles to 4,103,887. However its median Fmax fell to
83.114 MHz, yielding only 202.53 iter/sec. This demonstrates useful
overlap but also the need for a smaller queue and simpler head selection.
