hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate predicted instruction production from decode consumption
using a two-entry, fall-through queue. Preserve the champion's existing
agree predictor, direct-target policy, preselected recovery address,
single-issue backend and all ordinary instruction latencies. This is
one structural frontend decoupling; the predictor algorithm is unchanged.

The producer owns the full-width fetch PC and looks up the existing
predictor using that PC and the current raw bus instruction. Prepare
the complete existing if_id_t payload for each producer word: its PC,
instruction, direct_target, fallthrough_pc, admitted predicted_transfer
and preselected recovery_pc. Enqueue those values together on a ready
bus when space exists, advancing the producer to that word's predicted
successor even during backend holds. Do not advance sequentially past
a correctly predicted branch/JAL or associate a queued word with a
later lookup result. Store the prediction captured at fetch; training
after enqueue must not reinterpret queued prediction/recovery metadata.

Use two fixed payload slots, a two-bit occupancy count and a separately
registered empty flag. Select the raw producer payload when empty and
the fixed oldest registered payload otherwise. Wide payload selection
must depend only on this registered empty flag, not on a multi-bit
occupancy decode, backend readiness, bus readiness or live redirect.
Keep empty_flag consistent with occupancy: reset/redirect sets empty;
a push clears it; a pop without a push sets it only when the old count
was one. Occupancy gates producer capacity and handles simultaneous
push/pop. Shift slot one to the head on a pop and place an accepted
producer payload at the new tail; never overwrite an unconsumed head.

Empty-queue fall-through consumption accepts the raw bus word directly
when io_imemReady and decode admission are true, advancing the producer
once without enqueueing. If decode is held, a ready producer word is
enqueued instead. With a queued head, decode can consume it even when
io_imemReady is zero, while producer enqueue proceeds independently
when ready and space exists, including space freed by a simultaneous
pop. A full queue without consumption holds the producer. Never
enqueue an unready word, consume the head twice or lose a full-queue
response. The queue holds fetched instructions, not architectural
operands; source values are acquired through existing forwarding only
when the selected consumer is admitted.

Define consumer availability as !empty_flag || io_imemReady. Hazard
handling uses this availability for instruction starvation and raw
load-use eligibility, and uses the selected consumer's source tags.
It must not stop the producer merely because ID/EX is held. Derive
consumption from availability, absence of a real backend hold and
absence of correction. Preserve load-use flush-over-hold so injecting
an ID/EX bubble never pops its dependent head. Preserve MEM holds,
arithmetic drain/completion and every existing forwarding rule.

Accepted EX correction has highest priority: load the producer with
the exact existing redirect_target, clear occupancy and empty state,
suppress push/pop/direct consumption and kill younger decode validity.
A branch behind an older stalled memory request cannot correct/train
until existing EX advance permits it. Wrong-path queued instructions
cannot launch M-extension, access memory or retire. Reset cancels the
queue deterministically. Preserve empty bypass after correction so
ready-bus control-transfer recovery gains no extra pipeline cycle.
Keep raw/head payload visible independently of validity kills, as in
the champion's separate payload/control capture.

Keep nret=1 and every top-level IO/RVFI field, full-width modular PCs,
safe prediction admission, authoritative branch/JALR/trap behavior,
exactly-once predictor training, default-illegal decoder discipline,
real RV32M and ALTOPS, operand reporting, strict retirement order,
memory bounds and unchanged formal liveness/progress gates. Retain all
architectural tests; update frontend microarchitecture expectations to
distinguish producer PC/data from the selected consumer payload.

Project eight percent higher fitness with medium confidence from
hiding instruction stalls while limiting queue area and selection
fanout. The two-entry form requires independent measurement: the
four-entry probe's 8.2 percent cycle reduction is evidence for overlap,
not a claimed two-entry result. At 4,103,887 cycles, acceptance requires
median Fmax above 87.579 MHz; if two entries save fewer cycles, evaluate
the actual ratio against 213.40492 iter/sec. Main risks are queue
capacity, raw/head decode selection and routing of stored metadata.
Require unchanged formal, arithmetic suites, full trace cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/bounds checks and all three vendor
placements. Scratch artifacts are evidence only; recreate all logic
in permitted RTL and introduce no generated-file build dependency.

title: Validated carry prediction cuts the ADD/SUB forwarding recurrence
motivation:
The champion scores 204.02 iter/sec at 91.231 MHz over 4,471,643
bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path goes from ID/EX alu_b through
the EX ALU, EX forwarding, and decode operand capture back to ID/EX
alu_b. The accepted r10s2 predictor already removed most direct-control
bubbles and isolated recovery from that operand path; r9s2 showed why
adding late recovery to payload capture can lose the clock-rate benefit.
LESSONS.md is absent. The prior predictor log contains direction/target
prediction attempts but no arithmetic carry prediction. The promising
remaining predictor angle is to shorten the actual forwarding recurrence,
while validating each predicted carry before any dependent instruction
becomes valid.

A read-only run of the canonical 2K, -O3, ITERATIONS=10 ELF through the
unchanged reference ISS counted 2,922,016 instructions between markers,
915,184 eligible ADD/ADDI/SUB/AUIPC producers, and 236,980 immediate raw
source-tag dependencies on those producers, with no traps or OOB access.
A 16-entry carry-agree model predicting the carry into bit 12 produced
1,371 wrong forwarded carries among those dependencies. Each wrong
prediction needs one bubble, approximately 0.031 percent of the current
bracketed cycle count. Delaying model training by one, two or three
retired instructions left that count unchanged. These are retired-trace
models, not stalled RTL simulation or timing measurements. An independent
251,444-case arithmetic model covering boundaries and deterministic random
operands checked that a matching c16 always implies exact forwarded data,
and exercised both carry-error directions. The small modeled cycle cost
gives a clock-rate improvement a chance to clear the 4.6 percent gate.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one arithmetic carry predictor solely for ordinary ADD/SUB forwarding.
Keep the architectural ALU, memory-address generation, branch predictor,
registered multiplication/division, and producer retirement exact. Change
only the EX result supplied to younger decode operands for valid fast
register-writing ALU_ADD/ALU_SUB instructions, excluding jumps and loads.
This includes ADD, ADDI, SUB and AUIPC with their already captured alu_a
and alu_b. Other fast operations, JAL/JALR link values and registered
M-extension completions keep their existing exact forwarding candidates.

Normalize arithmetic as A + X + cin modulo 2^32, with X=B, cin=0 for
ADD and X=~B, cin=1 for SUB. Maintain 16 two-bit agree counters indexed
by PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6], initialized to weak agreement (10). Lookup reads
stored state using the fetch PC only; capture the agreement MSB with the
instruction in ID/EX, independently of payload-valid/control kills.
In EX use bias=X[11] and guess_c12 = bias XOR !captured_agreement.
Train agreement against the actual carry from A[11:0]+X[11:0]+cin,
only when A[15:12] XOR X[15:12] is 4'b1111, since only this propagate
case lets c12 affect the carry into bit 16. Enqueue one event per accepted
eligible producer, then update the current table counter on the following
edge. No live outcome or pending-update bypass may feed fetch lookup.

Construct a speculative forwarding result independently of the full
32-bit architectural ADD/SUB result. Compute the exact 17-bit low-half
sum low_sum={0,A[15:0]}+{0,X[15:0]}+cin. In parallel compute the five-bit
middle sum mid_sum={0,A[15:12]}+{0,X[15:12]}. Let mid_prop be the reduction
AND of A[15:12] XOR X[15:12], and predict c16 as
mid_sum[4] OR (mid_prop AND guess_c12). Compute the speculative upper
half as A[31:16]+X[31:16]+predicted_c16, retaining its low 16 bits, and
concatenate it with low_sum[15:0]. The predicted high-half datapath has
only a four-bit carry calculation followed by a 16-bit addition, rather
than waiting for the producer's full 32-bit carry chain. Its lower half
is always exact. Do not insert the authoritative 32-bit ALU result as an
ADD/SUB fallback into this speculative forwarding mux: that would retain
the original timed recurrence. Actual producer writeback still uses the
unchanged exact ALU result.

Validate predicted_c16 against low_sum[16] in the same cycle, before
admitting a younger dependent instruction to ID/EX. A carry match proves
that the entire forwarded 32-bit value is exact. If the carry differs and
either raw younger source tag matches the nonzero EX destination with EX
forwarding priority, insert one interlock: let the exact producer advance
into EX/MEM, hold the fetch PC, and kill the younger ID/EX valid/control/
dispatch fields. On the next cycle the younger instruction retries at
the same PC using the producer's exact MEM forwarding result. Do not
replay or retire the producer again. If no younger raw source matches,
a wrong predicted carry requires no bubble. Both raw source fields must
participate, including instruction fields unused by execution but still
reported by this core's RVFI contract; otherwise an apparently harmless
prediction error could corrupt rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata at retirement.

The new carry interlock must use raw imemReady and source tags, the valid
arithmetic producer and the carry comparison, independently of its own
flush-qualified fetch validity. Preserve every existing imem, load-use,
dmem and arithmetic hold. Suppress carry-bubble acceptance behind a
backend hold, and train only when the producer actually advances.
Preserve redirect priority; a normal eligible arithmetic producer cannot
also be a correcting branch or jump. As in the champion's recovery
integration, keep the new failure signal off raw decode payload muxes
and payload capture enables. It holds only the fetch PC and clears ID/EX
validity, ctrl, fast_write, mul_class and div_class. Payload may capture
the unaccepted speculative values but cannot forward, launch arithmetic,
issue a memory request or retire. Keep the existing load-use flush-over-
hold behavior. A failed prediction always falls back to exact MEM data
after one ready-bus bubble, so even adversarial predictor state cannot
cause repeated replay or compromise formal forward progress.

Keep direct branch recovery_pc and raw decode visibility intact. Preserve
nret=1, all external ports, exact retirement order, default-illegal decoder
discipline, traps and full-width addresses, real RV32M and ALTOPS behavior,
memory bounds, and every unchanged formal/cosim/CoreMark validation gate.
This is a single carry-prediction hypothesis; add no load-value predictor,
cache, fetch queue, branch-table redesign or arithmetic latency change.

Project nine percent higher fitness with medium confidence, primarily
from a shorter Gowin critical forwarding path. The trace model predicts
negligible added cycles, but actual stalls and queued training may change
its count. With 1,371 added cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax above
approximately 95.456 MHz; a ten-percent clock improvement would yield
about 224.35 iter/sec. Neither is a measurement of the proposed RTL.
The main risks are the new carry-validation control path becoming critical,
synthesis reconnecting the full exact adder to speculative forwarding,
and the unchanged exact memory-address path limiting further Fmax. Check
the vendor timing report and measured marker-bracketed cycles together.

title: Reset register-file validity instead of its wide data array
motivation:
The champion scores 204.02 iterations/sec at 91.231 MHz over 4,471,643
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior micro_opt
results favor removing control from wide datapaths; the r11 narrow-MUL
shortcut saved cycles but fell to 82.072 MHz and lost fitness. No logged
proposal has targeted register-file reset and storage inference. The
current register file synchronously clears every data bit and implements
two indexed asynchronous reads plus write-first bypass. A narrow reset
representation can preserve all architectural behavior while improving
storage inference, read selection and routing pressure on this FPGA.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the register file's bulk data reset with a resettable written
bitmap and a synchronous-write, asynchronous-read data array that has no
reset assignment. This is one local storage/control mapping optimization;
retain the reg_file interface, two combinational read ports, write-first
bypass, pipeline boundaries, instruction latencies and forwarding policy.

On a reset edge clear all written bits. On a nonreset accepted write to
x1..x31 update the addressed data word and set its written bit. Gate data
array writes with !reset so simultaneous reset/write cannot authorize a
write. No architectural register data array element is reset. Implement
the array in the standard vendor-inferable single-write/asynchronous-read
style; if two read ports require replication, both copies receive exactly
the same writes. Use portable RTL rather than FPGA-only primitive instances
so formal and Verilator consume the same logic.

Preserve each read port's exact priority: x0 returns zero; otherwise a
matching enabled WB write returns w_data immediately, including before
its capture edge; otherwise return the stored word if its written bit is
set, and zero if it is clear. The bypass must win over unwritten-state
masking. Reset must invalidate previously written words on every reset,
not just startup, and independent writes after reset must not expose stale
contents of other registers. Retain existing combinational bypass behavior
during asserted reset, while reset wins over writes at the clock edge.

Uninitialized physical words are unobservable because their written bits
mask them. This preserves the existing stronger zero-after-reset behavior,
x0 hardwiring and same-cycle WB visibility under all stalls. Do not remove
reset behavior from architectural state or change any consumer timing.
The intended benefit is a smaller, better placed register file with simpler
write enables and FPGA distributed-memory inference, increasing median
Fmax at unchanged CoreMark cycles. Estimate eight percent with low
confidence until vendor mapping and timing are checked; an additional
bitmap-read mask or competing ALU/divider paths could erase the benefit.
At unchanged cycles acceptance requires Fmax above 95.428 MHz and fitness
above 213.405 iterations/sec, not merely an area reduction.

Keep nret=1, every external memory/RVFI port, exact retirement operands
and ordering, decoder/trap rules, RV32M/ALTOPS arithmetic, bounded progress
and all memory/CoreMark invariants. Retain existing register-file tests
and add repeated-reset, unwritten-word, bypass-before-first-write and
reset-versus-write coverage. Require unchanged formal, trace cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/bounds checks and median Gowin timing.

title: Decouple predicted fetch with a single-entry instruction skid buffer
motivation:
The champion scores 204.02 iter/sec at 91.231 MHz over 4471643
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its frontend stops requesting new
instructions during load-use, data-memory and blocking arithmetic waits,
then must face instruction-bus stalls again when decode resumes.
LESSONS.md is absent. Relevant structural attempts are r10s1's four-entry
unpredicted queue and r11s1's prediction-aware two-entry queue. The latter
reduced cycles to 4135106 but its 87.761 MHz median Fmax yielded only
212.23 iter/sec, a 4.02 percent gain below the 4.6 percent acceptance gate.
A one-entry buffer retains most stall overlap with less storage, control
and routing around fetch, decode and prediction recovery.

A scratch prototype of this single-entry design, using the champion RTL
elsewhere and the unchanged FPGA wrapper and stall generator, completed
all three Gowin placement options at 86.846, 91.118 and 91.118 MHz.
The unchanged cosim harness ran the canonical 2K, -O3, ITERATIONS=10
CoreMark ELF with both bus-stall flags in 4212505 bracketed cycles.
All five required CRCs matched, Correct operation validated. appeared,
the timing markers were present, and oob was false. The resulting
216.30 iter/sec is about 6.02 percent above the champion. The prototype
also passed the unchanged retirement-differential harness on selftest
and all three committed random programs, both with ready buses and with
both bus-stall flags: 115, 11037, 11094 and 12059 retirements per run.
These are prototype measurements; implementation still needs the full
formal and standard evaluation gates. The prototype's option-zero worst
path ended at fetch PC through EX correction, rather than the queue data.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate predicted fetch production from decode consumption with exactly
one registered instruction payload and one registered occupancy bit.
Keep the empty-buffer combinational bypass, existing agree predictor,
direct-target policy, preselected recovery address, ID/EX boundary,
operand forwarding and blocking arithmetic handshakes. The producer owns
the existing full-width imem PC; decode sees the buffered word when full
and the raw producer payload when empty. Select wide payload only with
the registered occupancy bit, independently of bus readiness, backend
readiness, flush or redirect. No pointers, count decode, shifting or
additional registered fetch latency are needed.

Prepare the existing complete if_id_t payload for every raw producer
word: PC, instruction, direct_target, fallthrough_pc, predicted_transfer
and recovery_pc. Lookup the unchanged predictor using producer PC and raw
io_imemData. Capture all payload fields together when buffering a word;
prediction training after capture must not reinterpret its saved choice
or recovery address. Advance producer PC to that accepted word's already
computed predicted successor, not necessarily PC+4. Preserve the current
full-width address arithmetic, safe-direct prediction qualification and
actual EX correction targets.

Let full be the registered buffer-valid bit, I be io_imemReady and C be
actual decode consumption permission, after load-use/backend holds and
redirect/flush suppression. Fetch availability for the consumer is
full OR I. Define pop = full AND C, direct = !full AND I AND C, and
push = I AND (!full OR pop), suppressing all acceptance on redirect.
Every push accepts the raw producer word and advances producer PC once.
If push AND !direct, capture the producer payload and set full: this
either fills an empty held frontend or replaces a simultaneously popped
head. Otherwise a pop clears full. An empty direct transfer creates no
stored entry. A full buffer without a pop holds producer PC and payload.
An unready instruction bus never accepts raw data, while an existing head
may still issue and release the buffer. With a held backend and an empty
buffer, a ready fetch may fill it independently of that hold.

On accepted EX redirect, override producer holds with redirect_target
and clear full on the same edge; suppress consumption and enqueue of
wrong-path words. Synchronous reset restores RESET_PC and clears buffer
validity deterministically. Keep raw/queued decode visibility independent
of correction, and kill eligibility through valid/control fields. Preserve
the champion's isolation of correction from decode operand payload muxes
and payload capture enables. A load-use bubble must retain the head;
an older data request must stay stable until serviced; completed MUL/DIV
results must transfer exactly once before younger work resumes.

Drive the hazard unit's consumer instruction availability and load-use
eligibility from full OR io_imemReady, using source tags from the selected
head. Keep raw io_imemReady solely as the producer response qualification.
Derive C from the existing consumer holds and flush eligibility, not from
producer capacity; a full buffer can always consume its head when decode
advances. Avoid a validity/hazard combinational loop by using raw consumer
availability for load-use detection, never its flush-qualified valid.
Preserve flush-over-hold priority for load-use bubbles and the existing
control-only ID/EX kills. The empty bypass must retain ready-bus progress,
including the unchanged ten-cycle retirement-gap bound for DIV/REM.

Keep nret=1, external ports and RVFI fields, strict retirement order,
exact architectural source values, decoder-default legality and trap
handling, real RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic, memory bounds, and every
existing formal, cosim and CoreMark CRC/marker check. Change only this
frontend producer/consumer structure. Expected gain is six percent with
medium confidence, supported by the scratch timing and CoreMark result.
It trades 1.87 percent more cycles than the prior two-entry queue for
3.83 percent higher Fmax, enough to cross the acceptance gate. With the
prototype cycle count, acceptance requires median Fmax above about
89.90 MHz. The remaining risks are formal/trace integration mistakes or
RTL elaboration differences losing the measured placement advantage.

implementation_notes:
# Single-entry predicted instruction skid buffer

Implemented one complete registered `if_id_t` payload and one occupancy bit
in `if_stage.sv`. Registered occupancy alone selects buffered versus raw
decode data. Empty ready bypass adds no fetch latency. Producer acceptance
and predicted PC advancement are independent of consumer holds: an empty
held frontend fills once, a full held frontend preserves its head and PC,
and an advancing full frontend can dequeue without imem readiness or replace
its head on a simultaneous ready response. Accepted redirects suppress all
wrong-path consumption/producer acceptance, clear occupancy, and override PC
holds. Synchronous reset clears occupancy and restores PC zero.

Predictor lookup remains on producer PC and raw instruction bias. All target,
fallthrough, prediction, and complementary recovery fields are captured
together. Consumer hazard availability is `full_q || io_imemReady`, before
flush qualification, with source tags from the selected head. Predictor,
ID/EX capture and control-only kills, forwarding, backend/memory/arithmetic
handshakes, nret=1 ports, and RVFI wiring retain their existing behavior.

Deviation from literal payload capture enable: payload storage is clocked
separately from PC/occupancy. An empty direct bypass may also write the unused
payload register; a redirect may write discarded raw data while clearing
occupancy. These writes never accept an additional instruction. This removes
EX correction from the payload enable in the integrated core, while retaining
flush-only holds at the fetch unit interface. Initial literal push-only capture
had an option-zero critical path through correction into buffer payload.

Tests retain existing architectural checks and add independent producer/head
metadata tracking, empty bypass, fill/full hold, unready dequeue, simultaneous
replacement, saved prediction despite changed lookup direction, redirect and
reset priority. Directed pipeline tests cover load-use retention over data
waits, stable older memory requests, exactly-once MUL/DIV/REM completion with
unready imem, consecutive predicted JALs, branch/JALR correction, exact RVFI
operands/PC/order/traps, and absence of wrong-path stores. The ready-bus
ten-cycle retirement-gap assertion remains unchanged.

Local verification:

- Required Verilator lint: pass, no warnings.
- `make test TARGET=bench`: all 9 runners pass (99 cocotb tests, including
  32 pipeline tests).
- First full formal run: 53 passed, 0 failed; no counterexample or fix retry.
- Final formal run after payload-enable refinement: 53 passed, 0 failed;
  no counterexample or fix retry. Both local full formal runs passed.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` after building all committed random ELFs:
  pass, 5 ELFs tested. Selftest and random1/random2/random3 retirement traces
  pass with both ready buses and both bus-stall flags; CoreMark CRC validation
  passes under both bus-stall flags.
- Canonical CoreMark: 4,212,505 marker-bracketed cycles; timing markers present,
  oob false, all five required CRCs match, and `Correct operation validated.`
  appears.
- `NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench`: all three placement options pass at
  81.532 / 92.886 / 92.886 MHz; median 92.886 MHz; 5,044 logic cells,
  1,385 registers; fitness 220.50 iterations/sec, approximately 8.08% above
  the supplied 204.02 champion.

Concern: option-zero placement is substantially slower than options one/two;
the evaluator uses the median. Its final worst path ends in the predictor's
pending-valid register, and the option-one/two worst path ends in producer PC
through EX correction. No arithmetic RTL was changed; real arithmetic unit
tests and retirement differential cosim passed. Formal-deep was not run.

title: Validate parallel byte carry predictions before dependent decode
motivation:
The champion scores 204.02 iter/sec at 91.231 MHz over 4,471,643
marker-bracketed cycles. Its worst reported path recurs from ID/EX
alu_b through the integer ALU and forwarding back to ID/EX alu_b.
The agree branch predictor already saves about 302,000 cycles, so
further branch accuracy alone has little headroom against the 4.6
percent acceptance threshold. LESSONS.md is absent. The prior r11s2
carry predictor added only 1,164 measured cycles but lost clock rate
to 81.761 MHz, with a divider path becoming critical. Repeating its
four-bit carry preparation followed by a sixteen-bit speculative
addition and sixteen-bit validation would not address that risk.
A read-only reference run also found only 860 exact multiplication
operand-pair repeats in a 64-entry reuse model among 93,960 MULs;
result memoization has insufficient throughput opportunity here.

A read-only run of the canonical 2K, -O3, ten-iteration CoreMark ELF
through the unchanged reference ISS observed 2,922,016 bracketed
instructions, 915,184 eligible ADD/ADDI/SUB/AUIPC producers and
236,979 immediate raw-tag dependencies on nonzero destinations.
A model of the proposed three sixteen-entry banks and exact masked
training rejected 4,576 dependent candidates with one-instruction
delayed training, and 4,816 with two- or three-instruction delay.
One replay per such rejection adds about 0.108 percent to champion
cycles. This is a retired-trace model, not a stalled RTL measurement.
There were no reference traps or OOB accesses. An independent model
checked 50,330 boundary/random operand cases with all eight carry
guesses each: 402,640 guesses and 704,620 enabled training checks
passed accepted-value equality and authoritative-training assertions.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only ordinary ADD/SUB decode forwarding with one validated
byte-parallel carry predictor. Leave the architectural integer ALU,
branch predictor, memory-address path, multiplier and divider exact
and retain their current latencies. Eligible producers are valid
fast-writing ALU_ADD/ALU_SUB instructions, including ADD, ADDI, SUB
and AUIPC, excluding loads and jumps. The producer always advances
and retires its authoritative exact result, irrespective of whether
a speculative forwarding carry was correct.

Normalize addition/subtraction as A + X + cin modulo 2^32, where
X=B and cin=0 for ADD, X=~B and cin=1 for SUB. Predict the carries
entering bits 8, 16 and 24 independently. Use three banks of sixteen
two-bit agree counters indexed by PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6], reset to weak
agreement (10). Fetch looks up stored agreement MSBs using PC only
and captures all three with ID/EX metadata. In EX choose each guess
as X[7], X[15] or X[23] XOR the corresponding inverted agreement
MSB. There is no live-resolution or pending-event lookup bypass.

Compute four nine-bit byte sums IN PARALLEL: byte zero uses exact
cin; bytes one, two and three use the respective captured predicted
incoming carries. Concatenate their low eight bits for speculative
forwarding. Do not compute a preceding nibble carry or chain one
byte's computed carry into the next speculative adder. Do not mux
the full exact architectural ADD/SUB result back into this candidate.
All other EX forwarding sources retain their exact behavior.

Validate locally: predicted c8 must equal byte-zero sum[8], predicted
c16 must equal byte-one sum[8], and predicted c24 must equal byte-two
sum[8]. If all three equalities hold, induction from the exact cin
proves every byte is exact. Validation therefore needs only the
parallel byte adders and three comparisons, rather than a separate
sixteen- or thirty-two-bit validation carry chain. Reject the whole
candidate on any inconsistency; no partially wrong operand may be
accepted. Producer retirement never uses the predicted value.

On a failed validation with either raw younger source tag matching
the eligible producer's nonzero destination, hold fetch and inject
one ID/EX control bubble while the exact producer advances. Retry
that younger instruction using authoritative MEM forwarding next
cycle. Include both raw source fields, even architecturally unused
fields reported by the existing RVFI implementation. If no raw
dependency exists, a wrong guess needs no interlock. Qualify with
raw imemReady independently of flush-qualified fetch validity.
Preserve load-use, imem, dmem and arithmetic hold priorities and
correction priority. This eligible producer cannot also redirect.
Keep the mismatch off payload data muxes and payload capture enables:
it only holds fetch and kills ID/EX valid, ctrl, fast_write, mul_class
and div_class. Do not add this carry interlock to stall_id: on an
otherwise free edge the rejected payload may capture while its
controls are cleared. Suppress the new control flush during backend
holds, so a held producer is never lost. Invalid raw payload must
never execute or retire.

Enqueue exactly one training event per advancing eligible producer.
Train c8 from byte-zero outgoing carry unconditionally; train c16
from byte-one outgoing carry only if the c8 check passed; train c24
from byte-two outgoing carry only if both lower checks passed. These
masks make every learned carry authoritative without extra long
arithmetic. Convert each outcome to agreement with its X-bit bias.
Carry index, three agreements and three masks in a registered event;
on the following edge saturate the current stored counters. Consume
queued events during subsequent holds and support consume/enqueue
together. Never train from an unvalidated lower carry or a stale
captured counter. Reset control and counters deterministically.

This is a single arithmetic-carry prediction experiment. Its goal
is to shorten both speculative data and rejection paths to one byte
of arithmetic, with less arithmetic than the previous nibble-plus-
halfword scheme. Project nine percent fitness improvement with low

implementation_notes:
# Byte-parallel carry forwarding experiment

Implemented three independent sixteen-entry, two-bit carry-agree banks,
indexed by PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6] and reset to weak agreement (10). Fetch
captures only their stored MSBs in ID/EX; neither live training nor the
pending event bypasses lookup. A registered event carries the index,
three outcomes and three masks. Each advancing eligible producer queues
one event; the next edge saturates current stored counters, including
during holds and simultaneous consumption/enqueue.

Added four parallel nine-bit byte sums for ADD/SUB forwarding. Each upper
byte uses its own biased guessed carry. Three local comparisons validate
the complete candidate. Lower checks mask training so every enabled carry
outcome is authoritative. Architectural ALU results, memory addresses,
EX/MEM retirement data, branch prediction, MUL/DIV, ALTOPS and external
IO/RVFI remain exact with their original latencies and nret=1 contract.

A failed eligible producer with a nonzero destination matching either
raw younger source holds fetch and clears ID/EX controls/valid only. The
producer advances with its exact result and the consumer retries through
MEM forwarding. Raw imemReady qualifies dependency detection; backend
holds suppress the control flush. Carry replay does not enter stall_id,
forwarding selection or payload capture enables.

The forwarding mux explicitly implements the unchanged non-ADD/SUB ALU
operations alongside the byte candidate. This prevents the architectural
ADD/SUB carry chain from remaining structurally attached to decode through
an unused mux arm. No additional pipeline stage or arithmetic latency was
introduced. An extra captured subtraction flag was measured and reverted
because its median Fmax fell to 82.705 MHz; the final metadata contains
only the requested three agreement bits.

Validation:

- Required Verilator lint: PASS, no warnings; git diff --check: PASS.
- Local formal: PASS, 53 checks passed, zero failed, no formal fix attempts.
  The retained RTL passed after structurally separating the forwarding mux.
- Full cocotb suite: PASS, 11 Python runners. The subsequently expanded
  pipeline suite also passed all 34 cocotb tests. Existing assertions were
  retained and extended with independent carry-table and arithmetic models.
- Carry tests cover byte boundaries, extrema, wrapping, deterministic random
  operands, all eight guesses, authoritative masks, both biases, saturation,
  aliases, stored-state lookup, queued consumption, simultaneous events and
  reset. Pipeline tests cover correct/no-replay and incorrect/one-replay
  ADD/ADDI/SUB/AUIPC producers, both raw and unused source fields, x0, MEM
  retry, arithmetic launches, memory consumers, branch/JALR, bus holds,
  exactly-once training/retirement, and reset with held/queued work.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: PASS for zero-wait and stalled selftest
  traces and stalled CoreMark CRCs. CoreMark printed "Correct operation
  validated." with all canonical CRCs, ebreak=true and oob=false.

Final vendor timing was measured over all three placement options and
reproduced on a second run: [77.260, 86.633, 86.633] MHz, median 86.633 MHz.
Area was 5,344 logic cells and 1,367 registers, with 40 LUT-RAM, 4 BSRAM
and 2 DSP. The leading path runs from ID/EX ALU-operation decode through
byte carry validation to the fetch PC enable; the unchanged divider and
branch correction/control paths are also close to critical.

Stalled CoreMark markers were start=15,289 and stop=4,491,195, giving
4,475,906 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. This adds 4,263 cycles
(about 0.0953%) over the supplied champion. Measured median fitness is
193.55411 iter/sec, below the required 213.40492 iter/sec. At these cycles
acceptance would require more than 95.51804 MHz. Correctness passed, but
the hypothesis did not meet its performance acceptance threshold.

title: Flatten WB bypass and EX/MEM forwarding into one operand selector
motivation: The champion scores 220.50 iterations/sec at 92.886 MHz over 4,212,505 marker-bracketed cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The history records failed carry-prediction and register-file reset experiments, while predecoding EX eligibility previously improved clock rate. The current register file applies an x0/WB/stored-word priority mux before forward_unit applies a second EX/MEM/register-file selector. This serial operand selection is unnecessary: the four authoritative sources can be selected together. Scratch timing reproduced the champion and found competing branch, divider and decode-forwarding paths, so shortening one branch comparator alone was insufficient. This proposal instead removes a real mux boundary from both decode operand buses without adding arithmetic, state, or execution cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Flatten the existing register-file write-first bypass and decode forwarding into a single exact four-source masked-OR selection per operand. This is one local operand-mux optimization. Preserve the register file's storage, reset behavior, two asynchronous reads and synchronous write, and preserve every pipeline boundary, instruction latency, predictor and arithmetic handshake.

Add two raw stored-word outputs to reg_file, continuously driven by regs[rs1_addr] and regs[rs2_addr]. Keep its existing rs1_data/rs2_data outputs and their exact x0-then-WB-then-stored-word behavior for standalone compatibility and all existing tests. The core will feed the new raw outputs to forward_unit; its former bypassed outputs can be left internally unused and pruned by synthesis. Do not introduce a second physical register array, remove reset, or change write qualification. The raw outputs represent storage before the pending WB write; they must not include a WB-data mux or a read-data x0 mux.

Supply forward_unit with the current wb_w_en, wb_w_addr and wb_w_data as a fourth candidate alongside current EX, MEM and raw storage. For each source address, calculate nonzero = source_addr != 0. Compute EX hit = nonzero AND ex_wen AND ex_rd == source_addr. Compute MEM hit with the same nonzero and matching enabled tag, excluding EX hit. Compute WB hit with nonzero and matching wb_w_en/wb_w_addr, excluding both older-priority hits. Compute storage hit = nonzero AND NOT(EX hit OR MEM hit OR WB hit). Resolve data as the OR of the four 32-bit candidates individually masked by their mutually exclusive hit bits. Calculate tag matches concurrently, then apply priority to their one-bit masks; avoid a four-deep priority data mux. Implement the same logic for rs2.

The priority must be EX > MEM > WB > stored RF, exactly matching today's composition of forward_unit and the register file. A source x0 activates no mask and returns zero even with poisoned storage or writes to x0. WB must win over the old stored value in the same cycle before the write edge. A younger EX writer must beat older MEM/WB writers to the same register. Preserve current producer enables and destination tags exactly, including completed MUL/DIV selection, trap suppression, load forwarding only when operand capture is permitted, and invalid bubbles. Do not add a readiness, redirect, reset or launch dependence to candidate data or tag selection. Existing hazard holds remain responsible for blocking admission of unavailable load data.

Raw asynchronous RF visibility is harmless because only the masks authorize operand selection. Each admitted architectural operand, its ALU-input selection, store data and RVFI source value must equal the original two-layer network cycle by cycle, including stalled producer drain and result acceptance. No additional register, speculative result, replay, early arithmetic launch or change to fetch policy is part of this hypothesis.

The intended gain is removal of the serial RF write-first/x0 data mux before the decode forwarding mux, reducing LUT depth and routing on WB/storage-to-ID/EX paths. Estimate six percent higher fitness with low confidence: this exact candidate has not been vendor-measured, and EX forwarding, branch correction or divider paths may still determine Fmax. Do not claim the unsuccessful scratch arithmetic/branch variants as evidence of a gain for this proposal. At unchanged cycles, acceptance requires more than 230.643 iterations/sec, approximately 97.159 MHz median Gowin Fmax. Measure all scored placement options and unchanged marker-bracketed cycles; a smaller mux count alone is insufficient.

Keep nret=1 and the entire core IO/RVFI contract, default-illegal decoding, all trap rules, exact real RV32M and ALTOPS results, strict retirement order, arbitrary memory backpressure, forward progress, memory bounds and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker invariants. Retain every existing correctness assertion and run standard formal, arithmetic tests, trace cosim, canonical CoreMark checks and median vendor timing. Scratch files are observations only and must not become build dependencies.

title: Stream low-half MUL through EX and MEM instead of blocking execution
motivation:
The champion delivers 220.50 iterations/sec at median 92.886 MHz over
4,212,505 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The existing multiplier blocks
fetch/decode for operand capture, two busy clocks and completion
transfer. Previous reference profiling recorded about 93,960 MUL
instructions in canonical CoreMark. Removing two of their three extra
execution cycles could save roughly 187,920 cycles, about 4.46 percent
of champion cycles before accounting for bus-stall overlap. Independent
multiply consumers offer further overlap. No LESSONS.md is present.
Earlier narrow-operand immediate completion lost clock rate, so this
proposal keeps DSP products between registers and changes their pipeline
placement rather than adding arithmetic to decode launch.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give ALU_MUL, the RV32M low-half multiplication operation, a dedicated
streaming two-stage lane spanning the existing EX/MEM and MEM/WB
boundaries. Keep MULH/MULHU/MULHSU in the existing blocking registered
multiplier and keep the divider, integer pipeline, agree predictor and
single-entry fetch skid buffer unchanged. This is one structural change
to the common low-half multiply's execution/forwarding schedule, with
no extra ordinary-instruction pipeline stage.

In EX compute three unsigned 16-by-16 partial products directly from
ID/EX's already registered, fully resolved operands. Capture P00=Alo*Blo
at 32 bits and the low sixteen bits of P01=Alo*Bhi and P10=Ahi*Blo at
the existing EX/MEM edge, alongside that instruction's normal retirement
metadata and a low_mul flag. There is no additional operand-capture
register or busy state for this operation. Use synthesizable product
expressions with explicit widths so Gowin can infer DSPs. Ahi/Bhi are
unsigned bit slices; signedness has no effect on a product modulo 2^32.
No high-by-high product is needed for low-half MUL.

In MEM compute upper16=(P00[31:16]+P01[15:0]+P10[15:0]) mod 2^16
with a sixteen-bit carry-save compressor followed by one sixteen-bit
carry-propagate addition. The exact result is
{upper16,P00[15:0]}. Capture it as the instruction's normal MEM/WB
writeback value and expose the same exact value on MEM forwarding.
Do not append a 32-bit high-result adder or sign correction to this
lane. Keep the full original raw operands in RVFI metadata.

Low-half MUL has no EX forwarding candidate, just as a load has none.
Extend the existing one-cycle load-use interlock to a valid EX low-half
MUL with a nonzero destination matching either raw younger source tag.
Hold the fetch head and inject one ID/EX control bubble while the
producer advances. The consumer then captures the exact MEM multiply
result through the current MEM forwarding path. An independent younger
instruction advances immediately, and independent consecutive low-half
MULs may launch on consecutive clocks. Keep EX-first/MEM-second/RF-third
producer priority, WB write-first bypass, x0 handling and captured
architectural operand semantics. A dependent MUL-to-MUL or MUL-to-branch,
load/store, JALR or DIV consumer must obtain the exact result.

Exclude only ALU_MUL from the existing blocking multiplier's launch and
wait predicates; retain its high-half operations, saved metadata,
registered completion, acceptance and forwarding. This prevents two
owners of the same low-half instruction. A low-half MUL already in MEM
may drain while a younger high-half multiply or divide starts. A blocking
arithmetic completion may forward into a following low-half MUL normally.
Preserve old EX/MEM arithmetic-bubble and completed-result priorities;
an invalid bubble clears low_mul eligibility and cannot retire or issue
a memory request. Partial-product payload may remain harmless when invalid.

An older stalled load/store still freezes EX/MEM and the low-half
product capture with its metadata. Hold the older memory request stable,
then capture the waiting multiply exactly once when MEM becomes ready.
A low-half MUL in MEM is not a data-memory operation and cannot be held
merely because io_dmemReady is zero. Preserve MEM/WB clearing on genuine
data stalls, arithmetic drain semantics, wrong-path control kills and
exactly-once architectural retirement. Reset cancels all valid lane work.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS capture the exact existing MUL formula
(a+b)^0x5876063e into the EX/MEM lane and return it through the same
MEM forwarding/writeback selection and one-bubble dependency protocol.
Keep every high-half multiplication and division ALTOPS formula and
real arithmetic implementation unchanged. Keep nret=1, external ports,
all RVFI fields, legality and trap discipline, strict order, bounded
memory accesses and the existing formal depths/progress checks. Preserve
all real arithmetic assertions, CRCs, timing markers and UART checks.

Project seven percent fitness improvement with low confidence. With
93,960 immediate dependent low-half multiplies and no stall overlap,
removing two extra cycles projects 4,024,585 cycles and about 230.8
iterations/sec at unchanged Fmax, only slightly above the acceptance
threshold. Independent instructions can improve that saving, but saved
cycles may already overlap stalls. The short sixteen-bit final sum and
unchanged ordinary EX forwarding are intended to retain clock rate;
additional DSP placement/routing and MEM-to-ID forwarding remain risks.
This streaming lane is unmeasured. Require actual marker-bracketed cycles
and median Gowin Fmax to exceed 230.643 iterations/sec. At 4,024,585 cycles
this requires more than 92.821 MHz; do not assume the cycle projection
or a timing gain. Keep the unchanged ten-cycle ready-bus retirement-gap
checks, full formal/cosim gates and every existing architectural assertion.

title: Separate agree-predictor acceptance from late branch outcomes
motivation:
The champion scores 220.50 iterations/sec at 92.886 MHz with 4,212,505
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Previous agree
prediction already removes most direct-control bubbles; larger direction
tables or return prediction offer too little cycle reduction to clear the
4.6 percent acceptance gate by themselves. The two arithmetic-carry
predictor attempts lost Fmax. The current champion's option-zero worst
path instead starts at registered rs2, traverses EX branch resolution,
and ends at the predictor pending-valid register; its other placements
are limited by EX correction to the producer PC. Both paths currently
combine the resolved outcome with outcome-dependent misalignment logic.
Predictor integration should separate instruction eligibility from the
late outcome rather than add another speculative operand datapath.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the 64-entry folded-PC two-bit agree direction predictor, its
backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias, old-state fetch lookup, and the
single-entry predicted instruction skid buffer. Change the predictor's
event interface to carry acceptance, direction, bias and target alignment
separately. Queue an event for each advancing valid decoded legal
conditional branch independently of the resolved direction: candidate
acceptance is valid && !stall && !divider_wait && is_branch && !is_illegal.
It must have no branch_cond, misalign_fault, actual_transfer or redirect
dependency. Capture folded index, branch_cond, instruction[31] and the
branch target's alignment bit with that event. On the following edge,
consume it exactly once and train only when the saved target is aligned
OR the saved outcome is not taken. This preserves the present exclusion
of taken misaligned branches while allowing not-taken branches whose
unused target is misaligned. Form agreement from the two saved bits at
consumption, then saturate the CURRENT indexed counter. Consume during
subsequent backend holds and support simultaneous consume/enqueue.
Do not carry counter snapshots or bypass live/pending outcomes to lookup.

Factor the same predictor recovery predicate directly by instruction
kind and target alignment. Compute actual_transfer as decoded-legal
AND ((is_branch AND branch_cond AND branch_target_aligned) OR
(is_jump AND jump_target_aligned)). Do not derive this predictor predicate
through misalign_fault, ctrl_with_trap, branch_taken plus a second

implementation_notes:
# Separate agree-predictor acceptance from late branch outcomes

Implemented the hypothesis in `cores/bench/rtl/branch_predictor.sv`,
`ex_stage.sv`, and `core.sv`; extended only the two corresponding
`test/test_*.py` suites. No architectural or predictor-policy deviations.

`train_valid` now means candidate acceptance:
`valid && !stall && !divider_wait && is_branch && !is_illegal`.
It has no outcome, target-fault, transfer, or redirect dependency. The
single-entry queue captures folded index, resolved taken, instruction-sign
bias, and target alignment separately. On the following edge it updates
the current counter only when the saved target is aligned or the saved
outcome is not taken, forming agreement from the saved outcome and bias.
Consumption runs independently of backend holds and can coincide with
replacement. Reset clears all queued fields and initializes every counter
to weak agreement. Lookup continues to read stored counters only.

Predictor `actual_transfer` directly qualifies decoded-legal branch/jump
kinds with their respective target alignment, using branch condition only
for conditional branches. The authoritative misalignment traps, link
suppression, architectural `pc_next`, captured complementary direct
recovery, exact JALR target, fetch skid metadata, hazards, arithmetic
handshakes, external IO, and nret=1 RVFI retirement remain unchanged.

Verification:

- Required Verilator lint: PASS, no warnings.
- Local formal: PASS on the first attempt, 53 passed / 0 failed using
  `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`.
  No counterexample, RTL fixes, or retries were required.
- Full cocotb suite: 9 pytest runners passed. The final pipeline suite,
  including the additional unused-data-bus correction test, also passed.
  Predictor and pipeline observers compare all 64 counters and every
  prediction against an independent model of the old outcome-qualified
  enqueue semantics. Checks cover saturation, aliases, old-state lookup,
  simultaneous events, saved-field filtering, changed invalid live fields,
  reset cancellation, and consumption during MUL/DIV holds.
- The branch matrix covers all six conditions and both reserved funct3
  encodings, both outcomes and biases, aligned/misaligned targets, held
  branches, exact RVFI operands/PC/traps/order, and no wrong-path memory
  requests or arithmetic launches. Existing JAL/JALR and pipeline checks
  remain intact. Corrections are checked with instruction readiness low,
  and with data readiness low when there is no older memory request.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS for both selftest trace modes and
  stalled CoreMark CRC validation. Canonical CRCs and validation text
  matched; no out-of-bounds accesses occurred.

Measured performance:

- Stalled CoreMark start/stop markers: 14,543 / 4,227,048.
- Bracketed cycles: 4,212,505, exactly unchanged from the champion.
- `make timing TARGET=bench` and all-option vendor timing passed.
  Gowin Fmax by placement option 0/1/2: 84.177 / 87.325 / 87.325 MHz.
  Median: 87.325 MHz. Option-zero area: 5,079 logic cells, 1,387 registers,
  40 LUT-RAMs, 4 BSRAMs, and 2 DSPs.
- Fitness from 10 iterations / 4,212,505 cycles times median vendor Fmax:
  207.299 iterations/sec, approximately 5.99% below 220.50. This does not
  clear the 230.643 iterations/sec acceptance threshold.

The expected Fmax gain did not materialize. The observed limiting paths
include the existing ALU/forwarding operand recurrence and divider
recurrence. Correctness and predictor-state equivalence passed, but this
implementation is a measured performance regression. The requested
experiment remains implemented for the orchestrator's independent gates.

title: Remove synchronous reset from invalid ID/EX operand payload
motivation: The champion scores 220.50 iterations/sec at 92.886 MHz over 4,212,505 marker-bracketed cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior micro_opt attempts show that speculative carries, RF reset-validity changes and forwarding-mux flattening regress. Scratch timing reproduced the champion; arithmetic and comparator rewrites added routing cost or exposed the existing ALU-to-ID recurrence. The current id_stage synchronously zeros its entire ID/EX payload even though deterministic valid, ctrl and execution-eligibility bits already prevent invalid payload from affecting the architecture. This places reset selection and reset fanout on wide operand registers at the end of a timing-sensitive forwarding path. Removing that unnecessary payload reset is a distinct, smaller control mapping optimization; retain architectural register-file reset.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate ID/EX payload capture from the resettable instruction-eligibility state. Remove synchronous reset only from id_stage's raw payload fields: pc, direct_target, fallthrough_pc, predicted_transfer, recovery_pc, rs1_val, rs2_val, alu_a, alu_b, imm, rd, rs1_addr, rs2_addr and instr. Capture these fields whenever !stall, independently of reset, flush and fetch validity; otherwise hold them. Their initial or retained values have no architectural meaning while the instruction is invalid. Keep the existing payload capture permission and pipeline boundary for every non-reset cycle, including payload holds on load-use flushes and backend waits. No combinational data path, instruction latency or execution schedule changes.

In the same clocked module, reset || flush || (!stall && !in.valid) must clear reg_q.valid, reg_q.ctrl, reg_q.fast_write, reg_q.mul_class and reg_q.div_class exactly as today. Reset has unconditional priority over a hold, and flush retains its existing priority over a hold. Otherwise capture these control fields on !stall and hold them on stall. Every side-effect authorization therefore resets deterministically even if a payload field retains an old value. Do not replace reset with an initialization file, initial block, FPGA-only power-up assumption or added valid bitmap. Do not relax tests to accept valid uninitialized instructions.

The architectural register file, fetch PC and skid validity, EX/MEM and MEM/WB reset behavior, retirement-order reset, branch predictor and MUL/DIV units retain their existing resets. In particular this is not the earlier register-file validity-reset experiment: x0, all architectural register values and write-first bypass retain their exact reset semantics. Preserve complete architectural operands on every valid admission, EX/MEM/RF forwarding priorities, all bus holds, correction isolation, default-illegal decoding, alignment traps, real and ALTOPS arithmetic, nret=1 IO/RVFI, strict order and bounded progress. Inactive ID/EX payload must never authorize a redirect, predictor update, arithmetic launch, register write, memory access or retirement.

The intended gain is removal of synchronous reset from the wide ID/EX payload capture logic and reduced reset fanout/routing, especially on ALU/forwarding-to-operand paths. Project six percent higher fitness with low confidence until all vendor placements are measured. The same ready sequence and unchanged instruction scheduling should preserve 4,212,505 marker-bracketed cycles. Acceptance requires more than 230.643 iterations/sec and approximately 97.159 MHz median Gowin Fmax. Competing branch and divider paths and Gowin's register mapping may limit the gain. Require ordinary formal, unchanged pipeline assertions, trace cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/marker checks and all scored vendor placements. No evaluation-contract file or check may change.

title: Capture the low-MUL cross term with shared products at EX launch
motivation:
The champion scores 220.50 iterations/sec at median 92.886 MHz over
4,212,505 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The previous structural streaming
MUL experiment reduced cycles to 4,017,079 but duplicated product lanes,
increased DSP usage from two to four and lowered median Fmax to 88.485
MHz, leaving fitness at 220.27. The current blocking multiplier captures
raw operands even though ID/EX already holds their final values, then
spends separate clocks registering products and a final result. Removing
these redundant boundaries for the common low-half operation can recover
the cycle benefit with one owner and the original shared multiplier.
No LESSONS.md exists; structural history and the latest multiplier result
were reviewed. Scratch branch-comparison retimings were slower and are
excluded from this proposal.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure only the existing shared blocking multiplier around the
registered ID/EX source values. Keep the ordinary pipeline, forwarding,
agree predictor, single-entry fetch skid buffer and divider unchanged.
On accepted mul_unit start, capture the four halfword partial products
directly from a/b, which ex_stage already drives exclusively from
registered, fully resolved ID/EX operands. Remove the unit's redundant
raw a_lo/b_lo/a_hi/b_hi capture registers and products-ready phase.
The EX launch still captures the exact raw operands and retirement
metadata once in mul_meta_q. Add no separate low-MUL lane or DSP bank.

Keep the existing signed product decomposition: P00 is unsigned
Alo*Blo, P01 is signed({0,Alo})*Bhi, P10 is Ahi*signed({0,Blo}), and
P11 is Ahi*Bhi. Ahi has a sign extension for MULH/MULHSU, Bhi only
for MULH; both are zero extended for MUL/MULHU. Preserve the required
32/33/33/34-bit product widths and synthesis-inferred DSP arithmetic.

On that same launch edge also capture a sixteen-bit cross register
CROSS16=(P01_comb[15:0]+P10_comb[15:0]) modulo 2^16. Compute this
from the very same combinational product wires that feed the shared
partial-product registers; do not infer another pair of multipliers.
This places one short sum before the product register boundary and
removes carry-save compression from the following forwarding path.
For ALU_MUL, mark completion valid immediately after this capture edge,
with busy clear. Form the exact low result using just one sixteen-bit
addition: upper16=(CROSS16+P00_q[31:16]) modulo 2^16,
result={upper16,P00_q[15:0]}.
Do not route the low product through the full 34-bit cross-term sum,
the high-result adder, or another final-result register. The product
registers remain stable throughout a pending completion, so the
combinational low result is stable and is the only low-MUL completion
candidate forwarded to ID and accepted into EX/MEM on the next ready
edge. There is no unregistered DSP-to-forwarding path.

MULH/MULHU/MULHSU use those same captured products, spend one busy clock
on the existing full signed 34-bit CSA/cross-term and high-result sum,
then hold the registered high result valid until acceptance. Preserve
every signed correction and full-width carry in this high-half path.
Select between the registered-product low result and the registered
high result only with the captured operation. Retain the current
start/busy/result_valid/result_accept interface and simultaneous
accept/start support in the standalone unit. A new start may overwrite
products only when no completion is pending or that completion is
accepted on the same edge.

Keep ex_stage's blocking ownership, dispatch, saved metadata, completion
priority and EX-first forwarding unchanged. A low-MUL launch still
holds ID/EX and injects the normal arithmetic-wait bubble into EX/MEM;
the following cycle releases the consumer on the result-transfer edge.
No extra load-like interlock, MEM product lane, partial-product pipeline
bundle or new opcode bypass is needed. A pending multiply may complete
behind older stalled memory, but acceptance waits for MEM and happens
exactly once. Capture forwarded ALU/load/MUL/DIV sources, preserve x0,
cancel valid work on reset and never launch wrong-path or invalid work.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, keep all four existing formulas exact. Capture
MUL's alternate result on the same launch edge and expose the same
immediate-valid completion protocol; capture high-half alternate results
at launch and complete after their one busy clock. Do not introduce a
faster formal-only schedule, assumptions, changed formal depth or weaker
progress checks. Keep real arithmetic vector coverage and differential
cosim. Preserve nret=1, external IO/RVFI, all decoder/trap rules, strict
retirement order, memory bounds, CRCs, UART validation and timing markers.

Project an eight percent fitness gain with low confidence. Earlier
profiling counted approximately 93,960 low-half MULs; eliminating their
two busy clocks offers about 187,920 fewer cycles before stall overlap,
comparable to the previous streaming experiment's measured cycle saving.
Unlike that experiment, this proposal retains one shared product bank.
Acceptance requires more than 230.643 iterations/sec. At 4,024,585 cycles
this requires median Fmax above approximately 92.821 MHz. Measure actual
bracketed cycles and median vendor Fmax; retaining clock rate is essential.
Risks are DSP input routing from ID/EX and the sixteen-bit completion
cross-term sum after DSP products on the launch path. Require unchanged formal, arithmetic,
pipeline and cosim gates plus canonical CoreMark validation before
claiming improvement. Scratch evidence is never an implementation input.

title: Validate carry-predicted forwarding in MEM and repair held EX operands
motivation:
The champion scores 220.50 iterations/sec at 92.886 MHz over
4,212,505 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent.
Predictor history includes successful preselected branch recovery,
two unsuccessful arithmetic-carry predictors, and r13s2 training
eligibility separation, which preserved cycles but lost 5.99 percent
fitness. In r12s2, byte carry prediction added only 4,263 cycles to
its parent, but the critical path ran through carry validation to the
fetch PC enable and median Fmax fell to 86.633 MHz. This points to
the validation boundary, rather than prediction accuracy, as the
obstacle. The exact ADD/SUB EX-to-ID forwarding recurrence still
limits timing once branch-control paths are shortened.

A scratch branch-comparator prototype in this research turn passed
CoreMark CRCs at unchanged cycles but reached only 90.064 MHz median
Gowin Fmax, so it is not the submitted design. A read-only architectural
trace also found only 13,671 correct last-value guesses among 204,039
dependent loads for a tagged 64-entry predictor. The final hypothesis
is solely arithmetic carry prediction with registered validation and
in-place operand repair.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Use byte-parallel carry-agree prediction only for ADD, ADDI, SUB and
AUIPC forwarding, but defer validation to the existing EX/MEM register.
Keep the exact architectural ALU result on its original EX/MEM path.
The predicted result may supply younger ID operands; the producer
always writes its exact result, and a consumer may advance a memory
address, JALR target or branch outcome only after the producer's
prediction has been validated. No pipeline stage, retirement
width change, arithmetic shortcut or load-value speculation is added.

Add three 16-entry two-bit carry-agree banks indexed by producer
PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6], reset to weak agreement. Lookup uses stored state
only; lookup the selected decode head's PC, including a buffered head,
and capture their three MSBs with the producer before ID/EX, holding
them with its instruction. For effective addition operands X and Y,
let X = alu_a and Y = alu_b for addition/AUIPC, or Y = ~alu_b for SUB,
with initial carry zero or one respectively. At byte boundaries 8,
16 and 24, use X's bit at that boundary as the static carry bias,
XOR inverted counter MSB to obtain the guessed incoming carry.
Compute four independent nine-bit byte sums in parallel; upper bytes
use their own guessed carries. Concatenate their low eight bits for
the forwarding candidate. Architecturally compute the full exact
ALU result independently. Structurally separate the forwarding mux
from exact ADD/SUB: retain exact existing forwarding for other ops
and completed MUL/DIV, and do not leave an unused full-width ADD/SUB
mux arm attached to the decode forwarding data path.

Capture with an advancing eligible EX producer into EX/MEM: its
predicted forwarding value, carry-prediction eligibility, and three
local outgoing carry bits plus validation masks. c8 is authoritative
unconditionally; c16 is authoritative only when the c8 guess was
correct; c24 only when both lower guesses were correct. These masks
reproduce r12s2 exact training semantics without requiring a second
full-width carry calculation. Do not use any live carry-check result
to hold fetch, clear decode, qualify an arithmetic start, select raw
operands, or enable a payload register in the producer's EX cycle.
The exact EX ALU result and predicted value cross a register before
any replay decision affects the frontend.

In MEM compare the registered predicted value with that producer's
registered exact alu_result. If they differ and the current valid
ID/EX consumer's raw rs1 or rs2 tag matches the producer's nonzero
written destination, repair that consumer in place. On this edge,
allow the older producer to enter MEM/WB exactly once, inhibit all
effects and advancement of the speculative consumer, inject a real
EX/MEM control bubble, hold the fetch consumer and ordinary ID/EX
payload, and overwrite each matching captured rs1_val/rs2_val with
the producer's exact registered result. Also patch alu_a when its
matching source is rs1 rather than AUIPC's PC, and patch alu_b when
its matching source is rs2 rather than an immediate. Correct the
architectural raw source values even when an encoding does not use
them as ALU inputs, preserving the existing RVFI operand convention.
Patch both sources when both match. Keep every other payload field,
predicted branch choice, recovery address and instruction PC intact.

This is a one-cycle in-place replay, not a fetch redirect or refetch.
The repaired instruction executes normally on the following edge;
the older producer is then gone from EX/MEM, so repair cannot repeat.
An incorrect guess with no dependent current EX consumer causes no
replay. Correct guesses retain ordinary one-cycle dependent issue.
MEM forwarding and architectural writeback always use exact results,
so later consumers cannot inherit an incorrect prediction. During
repair, suppress consumer forward eligibility, branch redirect,
branch/carry training, MUL/DIV launch and result acceptance, and all
consumer memory/retirement eligibility. A speculative branch must
never redirect before repair. No speculative arithmetic operation
may start and then require cancellation. The held consumer has not
launched a blocking unit because its older producer was a normal
fast ALU operation; gate launches directly with repair.

Derive repair directly from registered EX/MEM producer eligibility,
predicted/exact inequality, nonzero destination and current valid
ID/EX source tags. It must not depend on stall_id, flush_id, redirect
or divider_wait. An unlaunched speculative MUL/DIV consumer already
asserts arithmetic wait and must still repair before its first launch;
using that wait to qualify repair would lose correctness or form a
control loop. A carry-eligible MEM producer has no dmem request and
advances independently of raw dmemReady=0. Retain actual older memory
hold priority for all other cases; these cannot coincide with an
eligible carry producer. Give EX repair-bubble and ID operand-patch
handling priority over the unlaunched consumer's arithmetic wait.
Override a load-use bubble caused by a speculative EX load: suppress
that consumer's normal EX effects and retain its validity for repair,
rather than clearing the held consumer through flush-over-hold.
On the retry, ordinary load-use behavior resumes. A branch correction
from the speculative consumer is suppressed while repair is active;
after correction of its operands it resolves normally. Preserve
independent skid producer acceptance while the fetch consumer holds.
Reset clears prediction/repair eligibility and queued events.

Train once from accepted eligible MEM producers using saved outgoing
carry bits and authoritative masks, regardless of whether a dependent
consumer needed repair. Form agreement with the producer's saved
boundary biases. Queue an event and on the following edge saturate
the CURRENT indexed counters; consume during subsequent holds and
permit simultaneous consume/enqueue. Never train from guessed lower
carries, stale counter snapshots or a repaired consumer before its
real EX advancement. Keep the existing branch agree predictor,
old-state lookup, training delay and recovery unchanged.

title: Capture byte branch comparisons at the existing ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 220.50 iter/sec at median 92.886 MHz with
4,212,505 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts
at ID/EX rs2 and ends at predictor pending-valid; recent experiments
repeatedly expose EX branch resolution through fetch correction.
LESSONS.md is absent. Prior micro_opt attempts flattening forwarding
and removing payload reset regressed, as did separating predictor
acceptance from branch outcome. A previously reported combinational
branch-comparator prototype reached only 90.064 MHz. This proposal
moves partial comparison across an existing register boundary instead
of merely rewriting the full comparison within EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming the branch comparator into byte-local decode predicates and
a shallow EX reduction should shorten branch-outcome-to-fetch and
predictor-training paths without adding a cycle or changing prediction.
Keep all existing pipeline boundaries, ready/valid behavior, ALU,
forwarding, arithmetic units and predictor policy. This is solely a
local branch-datapath micro-optimization.

Add two four-bit payload fields to id_ex_t: branch_byte_eq and
branch_byte_lt. In ID derive them from the final rs1_data and rs2_data
that are also captured as the architectural operands. For byte k,
eq[k] is equality of bits 8*k +: 8. For bytes zero through two,
lt[k] is unsigned byte less-than. For byte three, capture signed byte
less-than for BLT/BGE and unsigned byte less-than for BLTU/BGEU.
Decode branch_op[1] distinguishes these relational branch modes;
implement signed top-byte comparison using operand sign difference
and the unsigned top-byte result, with explicit widths. Equality
branches may capture the same harmless predicates. Do not gate the
predicate data with validity, flush, prediction or live EX outcome.

Capture these eight bits with the existing ID/EX payload on !stall,
reset them deterministically with that payload, and hold them on
load-use, backend and arithmetic waits exactly like the captured
operands. Preserve the existing control-only flush and flush-over-hold
behavior. Invalid payload remains unable to authorize side effects.

In EX compute equal = &branch_byte_eq and less = lt[3] OR
(eq[3] AND lt[2]) OR (eq[3] AND eq[2] AND lt[1]) OR
(eq[3] AND eq[2] AND eq[1] AND lt[0]). Use explicit balanced Boolean
logic. Select equal or its inverse for BEQ/BNE, and less or its inverse
for BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU; retain the default false branch condition.
Remove live full-width rs1/rs2 relational and equality comparisons
from EX's branch condition cone. Keep branch_taken, misalignment traps,
actual_transfer, redirect qualification, preselected recovery targets,
train_valid, train_agree and architectural pc_next equations unchanged.
JALR still uses its exact full-width addition and alignment handling.

The byte lexicographic relation is exactly the original 32-bit relation,
including signed extrema: only the most significant byte needs signed
ordering. Both comparator predicates and operands must describe the
same admitted instruction, including when operands came from EX, MEM
or write-first WB and when the held producer subsequently drains.
Training events, corrections, retirement traces and marker-bracketed
cycle counts should be cycle-equivalent to the champion.

projections, not measured improvements. Preserve nret=1, external IO
and RVFI, exact operands and order, decoder/trap rules, RV32M/ALTOPS,

title: Absorb data-bus stalls with a two-entry elastic EX/MEM queue
motivation:
The champion scores 220.50 iterations/sec at median 92.886 MHz over
4,212,505 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural
history shows that the single-entry fetch skid buffer succeeded, while
deeper fetch queues and faster MUL schedules lost enough clock rate
to miss acceptance. The frontend already fetches ahead during stalls,
but a stalled data request still freezes every younger ID/EX instruction,
even when it has no dependency on the held load. Short data-bus stalls
offer another place to overlap useful work without altering arithmetic.

Scratch probes in this research turn found that registered branch
correction and two exact carry-select layouts regressed vendor timing.
They are excluded. The proposed backend queue has not been measured.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single globally held EX/MEM slot with a two-entry elastic
queue consisting of a fixed oldest head and one younger tail. Preserve
the existing ID/EX, MEM/WB and retirement boundaries, single issue,
nret=1, ordinary execution arithmetic, predictor/recovery policy and
single-entry fetch skid buffer. This is one structural separation of
EX admission from MEM request completion; no cache, out-of-order
execution, speculative value or additional always-present stage is
introduced. With ready buses and an empty tail, the EX result enters
the head on its existing edge and retires at the existing latency.

The head alone drives every external data-memory output and enters
MEM/WB. It holds the complete request and retirement metadata until
MEM can accept it. Nonmemory heads can advance independently of raw
dmemReady; memory heads retain the current alignment/trap qualification
and ready handshake. A held head may accept one independent younger
EX result into the tail. Once the tail is occupied, hold EX admission
until the head can advance. On a head pop with an occupied tail,
transfer that exact saved tail payload to the head; simultaneously
append a newly accepted EX result into the vacated tail if present.
On a head pop with an empty tail, replace the head directly from EX.
Clear occupancy when an advancing entry has no replacement. Reset
clears both validity bits and payloads.

Select the external head payload with registered queue occupancy only.
Do not make dmemReady or live decode/redirect select a wide memory
address/data mux. Keep fixed registered head and tail payloads, with
head replacement and tail append handled at their register inputs.
Empty, held, popped and replaced entries must have explicit validity
and side-effect discipline. Each instruction is accepted once, each
memory operation is applied only on its actual ready handshake, and
each entry reaches MEM/WB once in order. MEM/WB may drain while the
head is held; clear its valid as today to avoid duplicate retirement.

Resolve decode operands with newest-producer priority: the current
admissible EX completion, the youngest valid queued tail result, the
oldest head's final MEM value, then the existing write-first RF value.
Run tag comparisons alongside producer data and use one-hot masks.
A queued nonload supplies its exact registered integer/link/MUL/DIV
result. A queued load never forwards its address. Head load data is a
candidate only when its response is ready and the access is legal;
otherwise interlock any decode instruction whose raw source tags
match its nonzero destination. Interlock dependencies on a tail load
until it becomes the ready head. Preserve raw source-value capture for
RVFI even when a particular instruction does not consume that source
as an ALU input. Exclude x0, invalid, nonwriting and trapping producers.

Preserve the existing EX load-use bubble for a current EX load, plus
explicit unresolved-load dependency checks on both queued entries.
Independent decode/EX work may proceed during a held head when tail
capacity exists; dependent work must stay held without capturing an
unready value. Existing accepted ID/EX operands remain stable and
exact during all holds. Do not infer permission to issue from an
unready load's transient data. The load-use interlock must let its
older load move into the queue while bubbling younger admission.

Keep branch resolution in EX on its existing edge. Publish a redirect
and training event only when that EX instruction is actually accepted
into the queue. Redirect flushes younger decode and the fetch skid
buffer, while preserving both older queued entries. When a full queue
blocks admission, retain the branch in ID/EX and emit no correction
or training; on acceptance emit exactly one event. A held older memory
request is never squashed by a younger branch. Keep the exact current
recovery targets, trap behavior, prediction metadata and predictor
update algorithm. Register capacity/occupancy and avoid loops among
redirect, decode validity, hazard holds and producer eligibility.

MUL/DIV may continue internally while a head memory request is held,
as they already do. Accept a completed result into available queue
space once, capturing its saved metadata and exact result; otherwise
hold completion stable. Ordinary EX admission, arithmetic completion
acceptance and branch-event generation share the same queue-capacity
decision. Preserve launch exclusion and existing busy-cycle schedules,
real RV32M and ALTOPS formulas. A busy arithmetic instruction must not
preserve/reissue an older head or overwrite the tail with bubbles.

Preserve nret=1, all IO/RVFI ports, strict +1 retirement order, decoder
default illegality and SYSTEM validity, full-width addresses and memory
bounds, alignment traps, byte lanes, source values and canonical
CoreMark CRC/marker checks. Ready-bus operation must retain the current
ten-cycle retirement-gap bound, including adjacent dependent DIV/REM
and branch/load-to-divide cases. Keep every existing check and formal
depth unchanged. Add backpressure scenarios that actually occupy both
queue entries; ready-only formal coverage is insufficient for these.

Expected fitness improvement is six percent with low confidence,
from overlapping independent execution, early branch recovery and
ready instruction-fetch opportunities with short data-bus stalls.
The oldest request still waits for its real bus handshake; estimate
gains from useful overlap rather than subtracting every dmem stall
cycle. This is an unmeasured projection. At unchanged 92.886 MHz,
six percent requires at most about
3,974,061 bracketed cycles, and the 4.6 percent acceptance gate requires
fewer than about 4,027,251 cycles. Measure actual overlap and any extra
dependent-load waits. The additional forwarding candidate, occupancy
control and payload routing may reduce Fmax enough to erase the gain;
score measured median Gowin Fmax times measured marker-only IPC.
